#2157. Barcelona's Anthony Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes' against Sabah as Spanish media hail England international on historic night

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 09:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 09:29

Anthony Gordon scored twice in Barcelona's 4-1 win over Sabah in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

In doing so, Gordon made history - the forward has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the England international's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice against Sabah on Wednesday.

Lamine Yamal missed out through injury, while Raphinha was rested from the start, with Gordon joined by Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus in the final third, and all three found the back of the net.

As expected, Gordon's performance brought a lot of praise from the Spanish media.

6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch

AS were extremely positive about Gordon's performance, saying that the forward was 'vital' to Barcelona securing all three points in the Champions League.

Mundo Deportivo also highlighted how well he combined with Gabriel Jesus and Adeyemi in the final third of the field in the absence of Yamal and Raphinha.

La Vanguardia concentrated on how Gordon became the main player in the Barcelona attack and said that he was one of the main reasons why Hansi Flick's side were able to score four goals.

Culemania said that Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes', having netted twice in the absence of the Brazil international, who has scored 19 times in all competitions this season.

Gordon will never be the main man in the Barcelona attack due to the presence of both Yamal and Raphinha, but he has played an important supporting role this term.

The 25-year-old's numbers for this season are relatively solid, coming up with five goals and five assists in 17 appearances in all competitions.

In La Liga, Gordon has two goals and five assists in 12 appearances, while he has struck three times in five outings in the Champions League.

The forward will be looking to improve his goal total in Spain's top flight, but it has been a positive start to his Barcelona career for the former Everton youngster.

#2156. Bucchioni: “Napoli? Finalmente si è ritrovato l’orgoglio di una grande squadra”

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Sempre Con Te è intervenuto Enzo Bucchioni: “Un voto alto per il Napoli, la miglior partita stagionale. Lo aspettavamo così dall’inizio. Una prestazione inattesa, finalmente però si è ritrovato l’orgoglio di una grande squadra. Si era visto in stagione qualche sprazzo di Napoli convincente. Il pareggio con il City ha un sapore differente. Non era atteso, può essere questa la ripartenza vera? C’è da augurarsi di sì. Le prossime sono alla portata. Il Napoli deve segnare di più e subire di meno? Secondo me subire di meno. È mancato il sacrificio degli attaccanti. Se non danno una mano per primi, qualsiasi fase difensiva va in difficoltà. È uscito Lang, la fase difensiva non la faceva, era pigro. Quando perdi palla devi andare con determinazione sul pallone ed è successo. La fase difensiva non funzionava per questo. Le squadre di Allegri hanno sempre avuto queste caratteristiche, ma non riusciva a farsi capire. Come vedo le parole di Allegri su De Bruyne? La posizione di De Bruyne la sappiamo, gli piace un altro calcio. Spero che contro il City si sia divertito, penso che ci sia stato anche un confronto. Un allenatore che si sbilancia lo vedo come segnale importante. Allegri ha ripreso la barca, quel tipo di calcio con il baricentro basso e rincorse all’indietro non faccia parte del bagaglio di molti giocatori. Anche Allegri ha provato a fare altre cose, ma non gli erano riuscite. Ieri abbiamo visto Allegri con la faccia giusta”.

#2154. Prosegue il tour degli stadi italiani di Marcelo Bielsa. El Loco è al "Penzo" per Venezia-Bologna

Continua il Marcelo Bielsa tour in Italia. Il tecnico argentino, che mercoledì sera era al "Giovanni Zini" di Cremona per assistere a Cremonese-Avellino di Serie B, questa volta è a Sant'Elena per Venezia-Bologna.

71 anni, Bielsa è attualmente senza squadra dopo aver chiuso la sua esperienza di tre anni come commissario tecnico dell'Uruguay, parentesi terminata nel peggiore dei modi con la Celeste eliminata nella fase a gironi dei Mondiali.

Da cultore del calcio, il Loco si sta aggiornando seguendo i campionati italiani. Ricordiamo che Bielsa fu vicino ad allenare in Serie A, ormai 10 anni fa. O, meglio, è stato formalmente allenatore della Lazio per due giorni in quella che è stata una delle situazioni più paradossali capitate ai biancocelesti.

Nell’anniversario dei 20 anni dall’incoronazione a Parigi, Fabio Cannavaro ha rilasciato una lunga intervista ai microfoni de’ La Gazzetta dello Sport ricordando il Pallone d’Oro conquistato nel 2006 e trattando i temi caldi del calcio italiano.

“L’Italia prende tanti gol, davvero tanti ma non è questione di coppia, bisogna ragionare di squadra. Devi far capire ai giocatori che non sono cavalli e il pressing deve essere orientato. Spalletti diceva “se perdi tempo tra il pensare di pressare e l’andare a pressare, sei già in ritardo”. L’Italia è così, siamo poco allenati a riconquistare il pallone e, se salta la prima pressione, fatichiamo”.

“L’Inter è fuori concorso per il livello della rosa ma aspettiamo. La Roma ha fame, un sistema di gioco definito e un attaccante che fa gol. Il Como non è più una sorpresa e sono contento per Gattuso: tutti pensavano che la sua esperienza all’estero fosse un tragico errore, invece è migliorato come allenatore e persona. Spero regga fino a gennaio, poi vediamo se il club gli comprerà qualcuno”.

#2152. Leeds United news: Major Dominic Calvert-Lewin contract update ahead of January window?

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:38

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has reportedly signed a new Leeds United contract running until the summer of 2029.

Daniel Farke's side have continued their excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign following the November international break, recording a 4-1 success at the Stamford Bridge home of Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

As a result of Lukas Nmecha and company collecting maximum points from the West London contest, the Elland Road club have stayed in seventh position in the Premier League standings, on the coattails of the Champions League conversation.

The main man in attack for Leeds in recent times, Calvert-Lewin has made a positive start to the season, with the 29-year-old Leeds star supposedly wanted by relegation-threatened Manchester United.

Nevertheless, the England international will be fully focused on helping Farke's troops qualify for European competition this term, with the Whites welcoming Coventry City to Yorkshire on Saturday.

According to The Athletic's Beren Cross via transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Leeds United supporters have been given a major piece of positive news regarding the future of leading marksman Calvert-Lewin.

The report claims that the 29-year-old has agreed to an extension of his current terms at Elland Road, with the Three Lions appearance-maker originally joining on a free transfer from Everton in August 2025.

It is understood that Calvert-Lewin's fresh deal will run until the conclusion of the 2028-29 campaign, at which point the striker will be heading towards his mid-30s and the twilight of his career.

Before Leeds can officially announce the news surrounding the forward, it is believed that they must complete 'formal steps', with everyone involved in the process expecting a smooth process in that respect.

Either side of the November international break, Calvert-Lewin's side have recorded back-to-back wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, proving their strength against some of the Premier League's biggest names.

Part of the furniture in the Premier League since the 2017-18 campaign, Calvert-Lewin has been the classic example of a confidence and purple-patch striker, with the attacker's form swinging dramatically.

This season, the 29-year-old is arguably churning out the best performances of his top-flight career to date, scoring five goals and providing one assist during the opening 11 Premier League games.

Whilst Leeds are known to be in the market for another striker ahead of the January window, there is no desire to replace Calvert-Lewin in the starting XI, as is clear with a contract extension on the table.

#2150. Napoli-Milan, prezzi e info per la vendita dei tagliandi

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

La vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

Ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN

I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE)

Dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM

Dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

Dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

In caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD)

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

#2149. Liverpool: With Isak and Wirtz, the Reds’ transfer business takes off a year late

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:44

During the 2025 summer transfer window, Liverpool broke the bank, spending £410m.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were the two most expensive signings, as the Swedish striker arrived for £123m (€145m) and the German attacking midfielder for £106m (€125m). But for many months, the two most expensive recruits in the club's history failed to live up to expectations.

In his first season at Liverpool, Wirtz scored seven goals and provided 10 assists in 49 games, but his impact was largely disappointing. Isak, for his part, barely played (four goals and one assist in 22 games) because of a fractured fibula. That summer 2025 transfer window was thus described as 'the worst transfer window in Premier League history'.

Both attackers were therefore expected to deliver in their second season at Liverpool, with new manager Andoni Iraola arriving.

The momentum is completely different at the start of this campaign, as the 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night in the Champions League illustrated perfectly. Isak scored twice, while Wirtz also found the net.

The Swede is rediscovering the efficiency that made his reputation at Newcastle United. He now has ten goals in all competitions in 16 games and has just scored in six consecutive away games for Liverpool. The 27-year-old is establishing himself as the number nine Liverpool had long been waiting for.

On Wednesday night, Isak was asked about when he would be back at his best level: 'It is always difficult to say, but I can definitely say that I feel good, the team is in a good rhythm, that is the most important thing' - he said.

After a season of adaptation to English football, in which he struggled to have an impact in the final third and to be decisive, Wirtz is in excellent form.

Still deployed as a number 10, the 23-year-old German has scored four goals and provided five assists in 17 games in all competitions for Liverpool.

His November has been excellent: three goals and two assists in three games for Liverpool, as well as three goals in two games for the German national team. Wirtz appears to have digested his huge transfer and to be ready to shed his 'flop' label at Liverpool.

#2148. Bayern, si ferma di nuovo Musiala: infortunio al al bicipite femorale. I tempi di recupero

Ancora brutte notizie per Jamal Musiala. L’attaccante del Bayern Monaco era appena rientrato in campo da un precedente problema fisico e nelle ultime uscite il tecnico Vincent Kompany lo aveva gradualmente inserito all’interno della sua scacchiera. Il giocatore infatti aveva disputato alcuni spezzoni nelle ultime due gare, il pareggio interno contro il Colonia per 1-1, e la sconfitta in Champions League per 2-1 contro il Lille. Il fisico però lo ha tradito ancora una volta visto che nelle ultime ore il ragazzo si è fermato per un nuovo infortunio.

A darne la notizia è il sito ufficiale della società bavarese che ha fatto il punto della situazione con un breve comunicato: “Lo staff medico dell'FC Bayern ha confermato venerdì che Jamal Musiala ha riportato un infortunio muscolare al bicipite femorale della gamba destra e rimarrà pertanto fuori gioco fino a nuovo ordine”.

Secondo quanto riporta TZ, Musiala avrebbe avvertito un fastidio alla coscia già lunedì. Adesso dovrà quindi intraprendere nuovamente un percorso di riabilitazione e resterà indisponibile fino alla fine dell'anno, si legge. Il suo rientro in campo è ora previsto per il 2027. Un ulteriore intoppo nel suo recupero e una notizia che non ci voleva per mister Kompany.

#2147. Conferenza Gattuso: “bisogna ringraziare i tifosi. Taylor non ci sarà…”

Alla vigilia di Lazio-Torino è intervenuto in conferenza stampa mister Gennaro Gattuso per presentare il match.

Alla vigilia di Lazio-Torino è intervenuto in conferenza stampa mister Gennaro Gattuso per presentare il match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Taylor non sarà della partita ha avuto un problema durante Lazio-Lecce, ha fatto risonanza ha un po’ di edema e poi lunedì fa risonanza con tutti gli altri e lo valutiamo. Noslin e Zaccagni stanno bene hanno fatto una settimana di allenamento con noi.

È motivo di orgoglio prima però complimenti a chi ci è sempre stato in casa, il tifo organizzato è una componente importante e da parte mia è motivo di orgoglio bisogna ringraziarli, poi dobbiamo essere bravi noi. Ho sognato dal primo giorno di vedere un olimpico da 50-60 mila persone. Domani sarà impegnativa, quando partono lo fanno in modo forte e ci sarà da battagliare.

Meritava molto di più di quello che gli ho dato ed è giusto che tante volte aveva la faccia arrabbiata, poi faccio delle scelte ed è così. È migliorato ha quelle doti che si sposano bene per la partita di domani. Deve giocare senza pressioni, deve mettere in campo le quali che ha ma gli ho dato molto meno di quello che meritava.

Oliver parte sicuro dal 1’ e poi sto pensando, chiaro che quando giochi con un destro sul sinistro può essere complicato però vediamo.

L’avevo preso nella mia ala protettiva c’è un grandissimo rapporto. Da parte mia c'è grandissimo orgoglio vedere come è cresciuto, gli auguro il meglio.

A livello balistico hanno tanti giocatori forti, noi abbiamo fatto tante partite sporche sappiamo cosa andiamo ad affrontare domani saranno importanti le transizioni.

Nessun cambio di modulo, proseguiamo  sulla nostra strada, possiamo pagare qualcosa a livello di geometrie ma la partita di domani si sposa in modo perfetto per gli interpreti che abbiamo. Le giocate che ti dà Taylor non te le può dare nessuno però facciamo le cose che siamo capaci di fare ci mancherà a livello geometrico qualcosa ma andiamo a mettere qualcosa di più a livello muscolare.

Bisogna continuare a fare risultati, a non subire l’evento, non possiamo permetterci di uscire dalla partita e dobbiamo essere bravi su questo aspetto.

è difficile perché ha avuto un risentimento dal 48’ fino al 93’, non ha detto niente, domenica ero qua a vedere la Primavera e c’erano 10 giocatori che si curavano. Taylor ha chiamato perché sentiva fastidio. Penso non sia gravissimo, però c‘è edema, penso non sarà lunghissima per le dinamiche.

Sutalo è un po‘ indietro, Tavares sta iniziando a spingere, siamo sulla buona strada.

Spero di starci il più a lungo possibile, ma le chiacchiere stanno a zero oggi è inutile parlare di classifica. Io vivo alla giornata e bisogna muovere la classifica dal Frosinone in su siamo tutti là. La classifica è bella, per i tifosi laziali e romanisti è qualcosa di incredibile ma ora dobbiamo fare risultati e muovere la classifica.

Il Torino con il Napoli fa una partita diversa. La rifà con noi o no? Noi l’abbiamo preparata ma non sappiamo come vengono ad affrontarci ma il dna rimane quello.

Continuare così, essere bravi a perdere meno giocatori possibili.

Doekhi e Leite sono di valore. Sutalo giocava nell’Ajax abituato a un calcio di palleggio. Contro Il Lecce nel primo tempo eravamo lenti non era un problema tecnico.

#2145. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Lorient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:21

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier said than done.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

L'Inter sa bene che per restare a certi livelli dovrà puntellare la rosa anche per il futuro. Se per gennaio si monitoreranno eventuali opportunità probabilmente soltanto per il reparto arretrato, in altre zone di campo bisognerà intervenire eccome per la prossima estate. Anche lavorando in prospettiva, come da tempo ormai sono abituati a fare in viale della Liberazione. Per questo motivo Beppe Marotta e Dario Baccin stanno valutando già diversi profili. #2142. Leeds United news: Whites midfielder 'close' to signing new contract following dramatic 2026 turnaround

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:57

Leeds United have reportedly moved towards agreeing a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka.

The Japan international has been a key part of Daniel Farke's side this season and started as the Whites smashed Chelsea by a 4-1 scoreline at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League last weekend.

Leading the line for the visitors in West London, Dominic-Calvert-Lewin is also supposedly on the verge of putting pen to paper on fresh terms at Elland Road, with Leeds closing in on the striker's renewed signature.

Losing just two matches in the top flight so far this term, Leeds are currently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings, with the Yorkshire giants targeting European qualification.

Aiming to record three straight league wins for the first time this campaign, Farke's side will be the heavy favourites on Saturday afternoon, when they welcome former Championship foes Coventry City to Elland Road.

According to Sky Sports News, Leeds are moving decisively ahead of a busy festive period on the pitch, with the European hopefuls aiming to resolve the long-term futures of Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka.

The report states that the Whites are closing in on a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Tanaka, whose current deal at Elland Road expires at the conclusion of the 2027-28 domestic cycle.

It is understood that Farke's side have offered the ex-Fortuna Dusseldorf man an extra 12 months of contract security, meaning that he is set to be committed to the cause until June 2029.

At the beginning of the calendar year, there was a real question mark over whether Tanaka had a future in the first-team ranks of Leeds, who were comfortably avoiding a relegation battle without the 28-year-old in their starting XI.

However, the engine-room enforcer has since fought his way back to the front of the plans for the Whites, with the midfielder starting nine of the club's 11 Premier League fixtures in 2026-27 so far.

Given the positive trajectory of Leeds over the past few years, it is no surprise that contract extensions are the talk of the town at the moment, with the club's hierarchy keen to tie their best assets down.

On the pitch, Tanaka and Calvert-Lewin have been key to the first-team progression at Elland Road, with the Whites looking set to establish themselves as a Premier League regular over the coming years.

Bringing Leeds back up from the Championship in 2025, head coach Farke is also in line for a new contract, with the German tactician certainly deserving of such a reward in the near future.

Adriano Galliani e Giovanni Malagò si sono ritrovati ieri sera al PalaEur per Italia-Turchia. Come sottolinea la Gazzetta dello Sport, a poco più di due settimane al voto il clima è più sereno, anche se ieri mattina, a margine della Giunta Coni, il commissario ha punzecchiato: «Che avrei fatto al posto di Galliani? Onestamente non mi sarei schierato, vista l’inversione a U delle componenti tecniche. Ma Adriano è un amico, non pronuncerò mai parole che non siano affettuose. Quindi lo dico col sorriso sulle labbra, anche se penso che questa cosa sia molto condivisa».

"E a chi parla di rimonta in corso verso il voto: «Mai stato in rimonta in questa partita, è una sfida elettorale come ne ho fatte tante, anche se con delle strane posizioni...». Galliani, intercettato in uscita dal PalaEur, ha detto sorridendo: «All’amico Giovanni rispondo che mi sono candidato perché l’inversione a U, oltre alle componenti tecniche, è stata fatta anche da 8-9 club di Serie A, tra cui grandi come Juve, Inter e Milan».

"Malagò ha annunciato poi con soddisfazione una nuova boccata d’ossigeno allo sport di base, arrivata in Figc nonostante tutte le incertezze di questi mesi: «Ringrazio il ministro dello Sport Andrea Abodi, è stato di parola e non era scontato. Lui e il Governo me l’avevano garantito, ora l’1% della mutualità che prima del voto di giugno era stato destinato alla Serie A femminile viene compensato dall’arrivo di 10 milioni per il movimento di base maschile e femminile e vivai». E il ministro, dagli Stati generali della Ripartenza di Bologna: «Stiamo semplicemente rispettando gli impegni. Il mondo dilettantistico aveva bisogno di un’attenzione particolare dal punto di vista anche della contribuzione. Sul Governo si può sempre contare quando il confronto è civile e rispettoso dei ruoli».

#2138. Man United urged to sign £62.8m midfielder to fix "phenomenal" transfer mistakes (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

New Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

"Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan said. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

"And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

"You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for big fees, who have no reputation.

"Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

"It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

"They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off."

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#2136. Bournemouth vs. Celta Vigo: How the Cherries could equal Chelsea, Leeds feat with Europa League victory

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly announced himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until New Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.

#2133. Luton Town vs Oxford United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the new season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells

Cumming; Kioso, Long, Brown, Currie; Brannagan, Andrews; Missanga, O'Donkor, Emakhu; Harris

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that said, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

#2132. Guardiola: “No alla Nazionale italiana? Mi vergogno, ma sentivo di dovermi fermare

Pep Guardiola, allenatore, ha rilasciato un’intervista a Romario a Romario Tv: “È uno dei miei più grandi onori che hanno pensato a me per allenare la nazionale italiana, ma sentivo di dovermi fermare. Se me ne avevano parlato anni prima, probabilmente avrei accettato, ma all’epoca, con Paolo Maldini e Leonardo, mi sono reso conto che dovevo fermarmi. Avevo bisogno di più tempo per me stesso. Sono stato allenatore per 18 anni, allenando ogni tre giorni. È la prima volta che ne parlo, ma mi vergognavo di aver detto di no a un Paese come l’Italia. In nazionale il tempo è limitato. Ancelotti? Lui si adatta a questi tempi più ristretti. Ma non potrei mai dubitare delle capacità di Carlo. È impossibile, perché lo conosco. È un leader nella gestione del gruppo. Dicono che sia il numero uno. L’ho affrontato, è molto intuitivo, intelligente nelle sue decisioni tattiche. Poi sa anche lui che se non vinci non duri. Il Portogallo deve dargli l’addio che merita. Entrambe le parti devono impegnarsi affinché ci sia un finale degno della sua carriera. Cristiano non può lasciare la nazionale portoghese in questo modo, non possono permettere che Cristiano se ne vada in questo modo”.

#2131. Cannavaro: “Gattuso spero regga fino a gennaio, poi vediamo se il club gli comprerà qualcuno“

L'ex capitano azzurro elogia Gattuso, guarda alla Lazio fino a gennaio e poi commenta la corsa scudetto.

Fabio Cannavaro, capitano dell'Italia campione del mondo nel 2006 e vincitore del Pallone d'Oro, intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport ha analizzato la corsa scudetto, soffermandosi anche sulla situazione della Lazio e sul mercato di gennaio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L'Inter è fuori concorso per il livello della rosa, ma aspettiamo. La Roma ha fame, un sistema di gioco definito e un attaccante che fa gol. Il Como non è più una sorpresa e sono contento per Gattuso: tutti pensavano che la sua esperienza all'estero fosse un tragico errore, invece è migliorato come allenatore e persona. Spero regga fino a gennaio, poi vediamo se il club gli comprerà qualcuno.

Palma? Ha grande potenziale, ma deve migliorare le letture e l'uno contro uno in area. Vediamo, di sicuro sa giocare a calcio. L'Italia prende tanti gol, davvero tanti, ma non è questione di coppia: bisogna ragionare di squadra. Devi far capire ai giocatori che non sono cavalli e che il pressing deve essere orientato. Back at home just days after PSG ended their eight-month unbeaten run on their own turf, Pantaloni's men will target maximum points to reclaim a European place, with sixth-placed Brest and fifth-placed Marseille sitting one and two points above Nice respectively.

That ambition appears reasonable given the Eaglets' three consecutive victories in this fixture and four wins in the last five meetings, with the visitors needing a strong performance to beat Nice at Allianz Riviera for the first time since 2017.

Stephane Dumont's men will fancy their chances of a positive result as they enter matchday 12 having collected six points from the last available nine.

Troyes' recent improvement follows a six-match winless run that included five consecutive defeats, with last season's Ligue 2 champions failing to score in four of those losses.

While a disastrous weekend could leave the top-flight returnees in the bottom three, that would require victories for Auxerre, Strasbourg and Angers, with the latter also needing a six-goal swing.

Troyes' leading attacking threats are last weekend's two-goal hero Antoine Mille and Renaud Ripart, who remain the visitors' only players to have scored more than once in 2026-27.

Merwan Ifnaoui faces a pre-match assessment to determine his availability this weekend, while Paolo Gozzi (hamstring) and Yacouba Kone (knee) are sidelined.

Premier League clubs are reportedly interested in signing Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown during the January transfer window.

With his performances catching the eye in Europe this term, Fenerbahce man Brown is supposedly admired by a number of high-profile clubs, including Nottingham Forest of the Premier League.

According to German transfer specialist Florian Plettenberg, Fenerbahce defender Brown is attracting interest from across the continent following an impressive opening to the 2026-27 season.

The report claims that a number of Premier League clubs are keen on bringing the 24-year-old back to English shores, with the winter transfer window opening at the turn of the calendar year on January 1.

Providing encouragement for those sides eyeing up a swoop for Brown, the left-back supposedly has a release clause totalling £19.2m in his current contract with the Super Lig powerhouses.

It is understood that the stipulation can be triggered either during the upcoming January or summer transfer windows, meaning that potential suitors have options in their hunt for the player.

The former Rams youngsters truly made a name for himself at Belgium side Gent before securing a high-profile transfer to Turkish and European giants Fenerbahce during the summer of 2025.

Former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia is an option to replace Bryan Ramirez at left wing-back for FC Cincinnati.

Tom Barlow, with 10 goals and five assists during the regular season, may also be introduced into the final third, but Noonan is not expected to overly-tinker with a winning team.

Meanwhile, Jack Maher could be brought into the Nashville SC backline after Maxwell Woledzi suffered an injury during the second half of the last game.

Yazbek and Bryan Acosta are battling for one place in central midfield, while Warren Madrigal may be recalled on the flank.

Sam Surridge, who has netted 21 league goals this season, has scored five times in his last seven appearances.

Although FC Cincinnati will be confident of making home territory count, we can only anticipate an improved performance from the Eastern Conference regular season winners. With that in mind, Nashville could edge this fixture by the odd goal in three to take the tie to a decider.

#2126. ‘I was distraught’: Ex-Sheffield United player has say on ‘disappointing’ Bramall Lane exit

Sheffield United cut ties with the striker following their last promotion to the Premier League. SUFC decided not to hand him a contract extension at Bramall Lane and he subsequently became a free agent.

Sharp, now 40, had three separate spells as a player at Bramall Lane. He announced his retirement in October but has since featured in non-league for AFC Rushden & Diamonds.

He has opened up about his departure from his boyhood club three-and-a-half years ago on Sky Sports’ Essential EFL Podcast: “I had a chance about three or four years before (to leave), Colorado Rapids were potentially going to take me but it wasn’t the right time. I didn’t leave Sheffield United. Sheffield United didn’t offer me a new contract which was so disappointing for me because I got told by the owners and by the manager three times that I was going to get another year. I got told on the day of the parade that I wasn’t going to get it which absolutely ruined the day for me.

“I was distraught. I was going to retire at 37, that was me thinking ‘do you know what, I’ve had such a good career and I can’t see myself playing for another team’. I wanted to end at Sheffield United but I was out of contract for the first time in my career and (then) LA Galaxy came calling.”

Sharp rose up through Sheffield United’s academy as a youngster and was a regular for them at various different youth levels. He went on to play twice for SUFC’s first-team before leaving for Scunthorpe United in 2005.

The Blades re-signed him two years later and he scored 13 goals in 64 matches before embarking on spells at Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Reading and Leeds United. Chris Wilder lured him back to his hometown team for a third time when they were in League One in 2015.

Sharp helped Sheffield United rise from the third tier to the Premier League and found the net on 116 occasions in 311 outings. However, his former club didn’t offer him fresh terms under Paul Heckingbottom and he subsequently became available.

As he has now alluded to, he considered hanging up his boots before LA Galaxy came calling. His stint in America was brief though and he later returned with Hull City before Doncaster Rovers brought him back.

Sharp will go down as one of Sheffield United’s greatest ever strikers. He is a legend at SUFC and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see him go back there in some capacity down the line.

The Blades are currently looking to claw themselves out of the EFL and back into the top flight if possible. They drew 1-1 at home against Southampton on Tuesday night with midfielder Sydie Peck scoring a late equaliser.

Wilder‘s side are sat in 9th place in the table after 17 fixtures and they are only one place outside the play-offs. They are one point behind Swansea City in 8th and could rise into the top eight this weekend if results go their way.

Sheffield United face a tricky away trip down to QPR on Saturday. Their upcoming opponents are positioned in 7th.

#2124. Conferenza Abate: ”Gattuso è come un fratello maggiore, lo abbraccerò forte”

Alla vigilia di Torino-Lazio, il tecnico granata racconta il legame con Gattuso e avverte che contro la capolista servirà maggiore cattiveria in area.

In vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la tredicesima giornata di Serie A e in programma sabato alle 18:00 allo stadio Olimpico Grande Torino, l'allenatore granata Ignazio Abate è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Sono d'accordo, ci sta mancando in questo momento. Diamo la sensazione di voler giocare a calcio e di voler accarezzare il pallone, ma le gare si decidono dentro l'area. Negli ultimi metri non sono solo gli attaccanti, ma tutta la squadra: dobbiamo prendere più l'iniziativa e osare per creare di più. Nell'ultimo terzo ci arriviamo, ma poi succede troppo poco.

Affrontiamo la capolista, sono forti fisicamente e di qualità. Sono intensi, bravi nelle ripartenze e nelle riaggressioni, e giocano con spensieratezza. Per noi è difficile, dobbiamo cercare di fare punti. Faremo di tutto. Gattuso? Per me è difficile trovare le parole giuste... Mi ha protetto, mi ha fatto crescere, un fratello maggiore. E' un piacere ritrovarlo, lo abbraccerò forte.

Sappiamo che per i punti si avverte pesantezza e delusione, i primi delusi siamo noi. Ma le gare vanno analizzate, io non vedo una squadra malata ma vedo la luce in fondo al tunnel. Ci sono aspetti positivi e negativi, ci aggrappiamo a quelli positivi per guarire quelli negativi. Tutti dobbiamo dare di più.

La difesa a quattro può essere una possibilità. Su Rodriguez non so ancora, mi confronto oggi con la società.

Loro sono intensi in tutti i reparti, serve una gara di carattere. Dobbiamo battagliare.

Non so se è una coincidenza o se in quel gruppo ci fosse l'attitudine a fare l'allenatore. C'erano tante persone con un grande valore umano, mi hanno trasferito valori che ho fatto miei. Molti di loro li considero amici.

Lo vedo in crescendo, mi ha dato grandi sensazioni. Per noi una punta fisica come lui ci può fare comodo: nel calcio moderno, quando ti aggrediscono, serve appoggiarsi su una struttura come la sua. Mi auguro che cresca ancora.

Dobbiamo essere coscienti dei momenti della stagione. Abbiamo avuto risultati positivi cavalcando sull'entusiasmo, poi bisogna stare dentro a questi momenti. Voglio qualcosa in più per far girare la ruota. Ripeto: lavorare in certe piazza non è per tutti, noi dobbiamo di essere all'altezza della situazione senza piangersi addosso.

#2122. Palmeiras vs Estudiantes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

After 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

In the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

Palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

Abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

Although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

In Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

Estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

Their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

Palmeiras’ medical staff are racing to get defender Murilo fit after he sustained a left-thigh injury. If he is unavailable, Bruno Fuchs is expected to join captain Gustavo Gomez and Alexander Barboza in the back three, ahead of youngster Luis Benedetti.

Forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

Fellow full-back Jefte remains provisionally suspended pending a hearing before the Anti-Doping Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-AD).

For Estudiantes, former Sao Paulo midfielder Gabriel Neves is still recovering from a fractured arm and is likely to miss out.

Neves joins midfielder Baltasar Rodriguez, who is suspended after being sent off in the second leg of the semi-final.

Joaquin Correa sustained a grade-two muscle injury to his right thigh against Talleres on November 7.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.

Miguel; Gomez, Murilo, Barboza; Giay, Freitas, Pereira, Piquerez; Arias, Roque, Lopez

Muslera; Mancuso, Nunez, Palacios, Rojo; Piovi, Burgos, Castro, Palacios, Cetre; Carrillo

With two solid, well-organised defences and goalkeepers in good form, a high-scoring contest seems unlikely.

Palmeiras may dominate possession, but Estudiantes could respond with a set-piece goal if they fall behind.

If the final goes to penalties, Muslera could have the chance to redeem himself after a difficult World Cup.

#2121. West Ham United vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46

Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.

Back in the Championship for the first time since 2012, West Ham United were expected by many to sit at the top of the rankings and waltz to a Premier League return, however, the East Londoners hit a new low on Tuesday night.

The Hammers extended their winless run to a worrying six matches (D2 L4) at Fratton Park, where a first-half effort from Odin Bailey was enough for Portsmouth victory, with the visitors once again failing to break down a stubborn second-tier defence.

Since the early-November arrival of Scott Parker to the managerial hotseat, West Ham have collected just two points across a quartet of fixtures, dropping down to 13th spot in the Championship table - a staggering 11 points behind first-placed Middlesbrough.

Following three away matches in their past four, the Hammers are back at their London Stadium base on Saturday, when Parker's men will be looking to halt a five-game winless run (D2 L3) at the East London venue.

In fact, West Ham rank 17th in terms of home form so far this season, with the pre-season title favourites last picking up three points in front of their own supporters on September 11, when Wrexham were hit for six without reply.

After placing between 16th and 18th in each of the past four Championship seasons, Stoke City have swapped midtable mediocrity for a Premier League chase in 2026-27, winning 11 of their past 14 league fixtures.

The in-form Potters have now gone seven games (W6 D1) without defeat after Wednesday night's impressive showing against Millwall, with George Hirst grabbing the headlines once again courtesy of a game-winning brace.

After recording five consecutive league victories for the first time since the days of Tony Pulis in February 2008, Stoke have moved up to second spot in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Middlesbrough.

The Staffordshire side managed just six league wins on the road last season but could equal that tally already with success this weekend at the London Stadium, where the Potters last played in April 2018.

That East London clash represents the most recent meeting between West Ham and Stoke, with a 90th-minute leveller from towering striker Andy Carroll forcing a share of the spoils following Peter Crouch's opener.

Looking for his first victory as West Ham boss at the fifth attempt, head coach Parker could make changes from the side that was defeated by Portsmouth.

However, there is little room for manoeuvre at right-back, where Joel Veltman should start in the absence of Kyle Walker-Peters (muscle).

Young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick could play once again, with Danish stopper Mads Hermansen dropped to the bench for the past two games.

Stoke suffered a major injury blow during the win over Birmingham City last weekend, with Djibril Soumare picking up a muscular injury.

In the absence of the influential midfielder, Jack McGlynn could start in a deeper role alongside fellow summer arrival Ethan Galbraith.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Piroe

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, McGlynn, Galbraith, Devenny; Manhoef, Bae, Hirst

Without a victory under new boss Parker, West Ham's ambitions of an instant Premier League return are fading quickly.

Stoke will be in the mood to take full advantage of a Hammers side devoid of confidence, however, we feel that a share of the points is forthcoming at the London Stadium.

#2119. Birmingham City set sights on La Liga attacker with talks underway

Birmingham City are being linked with the La Liga forward ahead of the January transfer window. BCFC have the chance to freshen up their squad with some reinforcements this winter as they eye promotion from the Championship under the guidance of head coach Chris Davies.

Romero, 26, is under contract at Sevilla until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal in Spain. He has made 11 appearances in all competitions this season and has chipped in with three goals and two assists.

Birmingham City’s Luis Vazquez is facing an uncertain future. BCFC only signed him four months ago but he has struggled to make an impact and is reportedly wanted by Racing Club.

Marvin Ducksch could also leave in January. Therefore, the Blues will need to bring in some competition for August Priske up top.

Romero was said to be on Sheffield United and Ipswich Town’s shortlist back in July last year. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put at Sevilla.

Birmingham City could see the Spaniard as someone to bolster their attacking department. As well as down the middle, he can also play on the left flank as well if needed.

Romero has enjoyed plenty of game time at Sevilla in the Spanish top flight over recent years and would be an eye-catching addition for Birmingham City if they managed to get him through the entrance door. He would inject more quality into BCFC’s options going forward.

Davies’ men will be full of confidence after their victory at Burnley. They will be eager for more of the same against Bolton Wanderers as they look to close the gap on Middlesbrough, Stoke City and Wolves.

#2117. Donyell Malen, 2026’s top scorer, on the radar of Europe’s biggest clubs?

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 12:02

Donyell Malen has been a new man since arriving at Roma. With the Dutch striker the top league scorer in Europe's big five leagues in 2026, can he join one of Europe's best clubs?

Struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan. The Dutch striker has stepped up a level since moving to the Italian capital, and he is enjoying an exceptional 2026 calendar year with 26 league goals.

That makes him the top scorer across Europe's five biggest leagues over that period, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe (21 goals). His current success has not gone unnoticed and led Roma to invest £21.3m (€25m) to sign the best recruit of 2026 permanently.

Malen has not been affected by the permanent transfer and is continuing on excellent foundations at the start of the season. He now has 12 goals in 11 Serie A matches, and must also add five goals and two assists in five Champions League matches.

The versatile forward, who was often used on the flanks at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, has been installed as the number nine by Gian Piero Gasperini with great success.

The Dutchman's performances are logically starting to attract more prestigious suitors.

With Kane injured at Bayern Munich and Doue and Kvaratskhelia injured at PSG, Malen's name has been cited as a target for both giants.

The two-time European champions are looking for a versatile forward for January, which is exactly what Malen is. His profile fits Paris's needs.

However, PSG do not want to overpay, and as things stand Roma have no interest in selling their star man, who is under contract until June 2030, in the middle of the season unless an exceptional offer arrives. A transfer in January therefore looks very unlikely, even to Bayern Munich, where he would also make a lot of sense with Kane absent for several months.

On the other hand, if Malen continues in this vein, the approaches should multiply next summer. A move to one of Europe's heavyweights could also appeal to the Roma forward, with the Italian club potentially struggling to keep hold of him and to turn down huge offers.

#2115. Bromley vs Burton Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that said, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

#2112. Update emerges on future of Manchester City’s goalkeepers – it could impact QPR and Pierce Charles

QPR signed Pierce Charles on loan from Manchester City in the summer, following his switch from Sheffield Wednesday to the Premier League giants. The 20-year-old was viewed as a big talent before this season, but his starring performances for the Hoops have put the wider footballing world on notice.

As Charles impresses at Loftus Road, change could await in the goalkeeping department back at his parent club. The Athletic tips Manchester City to make changes in between the sticks by moving out both Gianluigi Donnarumma and backup Geronimo Rulli in 2027.

Rulli, 34, is only cover, but Donnarumma has drawn criticism for his shortcomings in possession, given that City need a goalkeeper who is comfortable in helping in build-up phases. This is undoubtedly Charles’ standout attribute, and it may well see him accelerated into first-team contention at the Etihad Stadium.

To make it clear, there is nothing suggested about a Charles recall from QPR in The Athletic’s new report. In October, it was confirmed that Manchester City have an option to bring him back in January if they wish, but there were no plans at the time.

Regular EFL viewers have known about Charles’ potential for some time. He emerged on the first-team stage at Sheffield Wednesday and quickly impressed with his distribution, showing composure beyond his years and a passing range that wouldn’t look out of place in midfield.

Those same attributes in possession have been on show with the Hoops, but Charles is growing in confidence in commanding his box and claiming crosses too. A save percentage of 67.8% shows there is still room for improvement with regard to shot-stopping (FotMob).

However, Charles’ passing abilities make him an ideal fit for Manchester City’s style, and he seems bound to get a chance in the future. Accuracy is one thing, but the Northern Irishman’s technique sees means he can play flat balls into the attackers too, allowing them to bring it down on their chest or with their feet rather than challenging for headers with big Championship centre-backs.

This allows QPR to get the ball forward quickly and keep it there. It is a rare ability in goalkeepers, and one that will not go unnoticed at Manchester City.

Manchester City need a goalkeeper comfortable in build-up, and Charles is just that. However, at this moment in time, it would be a big risk to pull him from his QPR loan and throw him into the starting lineup.

As touched on before, his save percentage shows he still needs to improve as a shot-stopper. The progress he is making in West London suggests he can grow and become a starting option for City further down the line, but at present, the areas he still has to improve could be exposed at an elite level.

It means the Hoops should be confident of keeping Charles for the season – it would be best for him to stay for the full campaign too.

However, in the interest of staying prepared, it might be wise for the R’s to eye potential replacements. That way, if Manchester City do make a bold move to recall Charles, they are ready to act swiftly when January comes around.
