#2107. Millwall vs Burnley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18

Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.

The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.

After suffering just four Championship away defeats last season on their way to a third-placed finish, Millwall picked up their sixth loss on the road in 2026-27 at Stoke on Wednesday night.

The Lions extended their losing run to four consecutive matches following a lacklustre first-half display at the bet365 Stadium, where in-form striker George Hirst bagged a game-clinching brace for the hosts.

Winning just one of their past eight second-tier matches (D1 L6), Alex Neil's side have plummeted down to 18th spot in the Championship standings, a mammoth nine points behind the current top-eight pace.

Following four straight losses on the road, Millwall are in desperate need of some home comforts this weekend; however, the Lions have enjoyed victory in just one of their past six (D2 L3) competitive contests at The Den.

One of a multitude of problems facing head coach Neil ahead of a hectic festive period, the South Londoners are struggling in attack since the summer departure of Femi Azeez, scoring only once across their past four matches.

Whilst Millwall are experiencing a saddening fall from grace relative to last season, Saturday's visitors Burnley are in the midst of a full-blown crisis, with the recently-relegated side currently sleepwalking towards League One.

A 2-0 defeat by Birmingham at Turf Moor on Wednesday night made it 24 consecutive home league fixtures without a win for the Clarets - the longest such streak in the history of English football.

Despite this, head coach Fabio Celestini opted for the glass-half-full approach during his post-match media duties, insisting that Burnley bested Blues outside of the two boxes during the Lancashire loss.

The optimistic Swiss boss needs to increase his side's effectiveness in the decisive moments to avoid the same fate as Nicky Hayen, though, as the Clarets are winless in their opening five matches (D3 L2) with the 51-year-old at the helm.

Joining Premier League strugglers Manchester United on just the single league victory so far this season, Burnley are currently occupying 23rd position in the Championship rankings, four points from safety.

After accusing a number of his players of "not taking part in the game" at Stoke on Wednesday, it is safe to say that Millwall boss Neil is planning changes to his XI this weekend.

That indirect jab was likely commenting on the displays of Milhailo Ivanovic, Tairyk Arconte and Jenson Metcalfe, with the trio replaced at half time.

Derek Mazou-Sacko will start in the middle of the park, and influential Belgian Casper de Norre is set to return to the matchday squad.

Zak Sturge's absence reduces the hosts' options at left-back, with the 22-year-old picking up a straight red card during the defeat by Queens Park Rangers last Saturday.

Burnley also have a suspended player for this weekend's clash, with Wales international Connor Roberts out of action following his dismissal at Cardiff City on November 7.

The Clarets could make attacking alterations after firing a blank against Birmingham, with Marcus Edwards and Jamie Vardy pushing for starts.

#2106. John Eustace must consider dropping struggling 26-year-old from Derby County starting XI vs Watford: Opinion

Derby County are rooted to the bottom of the Championship table coming into this weekend’s games, and there is huge pressure on head coach John Eustace. However, he remains in post and will lead DCFC for their home game against fellow strugglers Watford on Saturday.

It feels like a must-win match for Eustace, who has been under growing pressure from supporters. The season has been a tough one all-round at Pride Park, but with 35 goals conceded in 17 games, they have the joint-worst defence in the league.

One man who has been near ever-present in the Rams’ struggling backline is Dion Sanderson. Against Watford, Eustace has to consider pulling the 26-year-old from the starting lineup.

Sanderson has made 15 Championship appearances this season, starting all of them. He has played the full 90 minutes on all but two occasions, being taken off at half-time against West Brom and seeing red after 66 minutes in the 1-1 draw against Sheffield United.

Sanderson was a hit with Derby County last season and he has proven his ability in the Championship across 169 appearances at the level, so Eustace has good reason to believe the defender can deliver. However, the facts are that he hasn’t this season.

The former Birmingham City man has won only 51.3% of his duels, ranking him in the bottom 17% of Championship defenders. DCFC have conceded 28.13 xG with Sanderson on the pitch (bottom 2%) as well, although this is more of an indication of how bad the backline has been as a unit (FotMob).

Eustace has been limited in his ability to make defensive changes, but that is not the case anymore.

Matt Clarke returned to the team against Wolves, and Eiran Cashin was back on the bench. Those two, alongside free transfer signings Shane Duffy and Jack Robinson, mean that Derby County have the depth to make alterations in a bid to find form.

Duffy has impressed since joining, so it could be him and Clarke started in a centre-back pairing. If Eustace goes for a three at the back, it should be the fit-again Cashin or Robinson to join them in the side, not Sanderson.

Derby County desperately need some hope. The 3-1 win over Bolton Wanderers gave them a boost, but consecutive defeats to Southampton and Wolves have dampened spirits again.

As rival clubs make changes in the dugout, DCFC have stuck by Eustace. However, that could change with a home defeat to Watford.

This is a winnable game, and you get the feeling that three points are a must. If not, Eustace could be sacked.

That could prompt changes from the boss, who will do all he can to drive a performance from his struggling side as pressure and relegation fears grow.

#2105. Bayern, Kompany: "Pronto a una corsa per il titolo combattuta. Con l'Amburgo sarà speciale"

Intervenuto in conferenza stampa, il tecnico del Bayern Monaco Vincent Kompany ha parlato della sfida contro l'Amburgo: "Sarà sempre una partita speciale per me. Non so bene perché: non ci sono rimasto così a lungo, ma la città e la gente ti lasciano qualcosa dentro. Abbiamo una motivazione in più per conquistare i tre punti, dato che al momento stiamo affrontando delle sfide. Quindi, la partita non è carica di emozioni solo per il mio passato, ma anche per la storia della nostra squadra. Vogliamo andare ad Amburgo insieme ai nostri tifosi e dimostrare che stiamo facendo tutto il possibile. Per quanto riguarda ciò che sfugge al nostro controllo, beh, su quello non possiamo influire.

Come allenatore, devi dare l'esempio. L'ho fatto per tutta la mia carriera e non inizierò a fare diversamente proprio oggi. Credo in questo approccio e voglio dimostrare che conta solo l'aspetto sportivo. Se i singoli giocatori possono essere influenzati, proprio come chiunque altro, il che è del tutto normale, allora spero che il nostro ambiente possa aiutare a invertire la rotta. Se domani giochiamo bene, tutto tornerà a posto. Per un calciatore, questa è una dote fondamentale, che richiede tempo per essere appresa.

La corsa al titolo? Sono sempre pronto a una corsa al titolo combattuta, fin dall'inizio. Il Leverkusen ha ottenuto 90 punti: una sfida del genere sarebbe stata durissima per qualsiasi generazione del Bayern. Solo in un'occasione, in uno scenario simile, avremmo vinto noi il titolo; noi stabilimmo il record con 91 punti. Se un'altra squadra è così forte, allora sia così. Ma noi ci concentriamo solo su ciò che possiamo controllare".

Manchester United have been handed a potential boost in their pursuit of Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, who is reportedly keen on a move to Old Trafford.

The Uruguay international caught the attention of United officials during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon, having been monitored by the club for several months.

However, a potential January deal could prove difficult given the asking price and Mauricio Pochettino's limited transfer budget.

According to Sport Witness, a source close to the situation has indicated that Araujo 'wants to join' United, with mutual appreciation between the player and the Premier League outfit.

However, it's believed a fee closer to £50m could actually be enough to secure his services in the January transfer window, despite his new contract and substantial salary in Portugal.

United officials reportedly watched him closely during Wednesday's Champions League meeting, with Araujo playing the full 90 minutes.

The left-back has made 15 appearances this season and is viewed as a potential solution to United's problems in the position.

Luke Shaw has missed the last eight matches with a muscle injury, while youngster Harry Amass is also among the club's recognised options. Both players have contracts expiring in 2027, adding further uncertainty to the position.

Araujo's performance against United offered Pochettino an opportunity to assess a potential transfer target at close quarters.

Operating in an advanced left wing-back role, the Uruguayan registered two shots, created one chance, won three fouls and completed six progressive passes. He also made six defensive contributions, including three interceptions, per Sofascore.

It was not necessarily a spectacular individual display, but his all-round contribution attracted praise from the Portuguese press and demonstrated the qualities United could benefit from on the left flank.

Araujo could provide the attacking thrust and defensive work rate required to solve a problem position, although the financial implications are significant.

A reported £50m asking price would represent a sizeable investment, particularly with United believed to have less than that available for multiple positions in January.

Pochettino may be impressed by what he saw in Lisbon, but convincing the hierarchy to spend such a large proportion of their budget on one full-back could be difficult when central defence and striker reinforcements are also needed.

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:37

Preston North End play host to Norwich City on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that could move them outside of the relegation zone.

At a time when the home side sit in 22nd place in the Championship table, Norwich remain in 11th position despite their prolonged unbeaten streak.

While many questioned why Graham Alexander left a League One promotion bid with Bradford for a relegation scrap at Deepdale, the Preston legend is currently justifying his decision.

Seven points have been accumulated across the last three fixtures against Southampton, West Ham United and Cardiff City.

Preston had been heavy underdogs in all three contests, yet they came through that triple-header having conceded just the one goal.

Although Preston had to battle hard to earn a share of the spoils at West Ham on Saturday, they were ruthless in dispatching Cardiff by a 4-0 scoreline in South Wales three days later.

Despite remaining three points adrift of safety, confidence is growing at Preston ahead of facing one of the form teams in the division.

Such has been the upturn in Norwich's fortunes that they were disappointed to record a 1-1 draw at home to Queens Park Rangers in midweek.

Nevertheless, having won their previous five games, it extended their recent return to 16 points from a possible 18.

Philippe Clement's side remain with three points of sixth-placed Southampton, a position they will take having lost eight of their opening 11 league matches this season.

Norwich have scored 19 goals in eight away fixtures, the joint-best attacking record in the division, while they have won their most recent three contests away from Carrow Road.

Barring any fitness issues, Preston boss Alexander is expected to name the same starting lineup from the Cardiff game.

Preston were 4-0 ahead before substitutions were first made in the 77th minute, and the same players should keep their places.

The likes of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson and Liam Gibbs are all expected to remain sidelined.

Meanwhile, Kenny McLean, Anis Ben Slimane, Oscar Schwartau and Jovon Makama are all in contention for opportunities in the Norwich XI.

Jacob Wright, Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden could be the players to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

#2100. Ds Sassuolo: "Napoli forte ma vogliamo rialzarci. Il club a gennaio non vende i big"

Il Sassuolo ha voglia di ripartire. La 13^ giornata di Serie A porta il Napoli al Mapei Stadium, con i neroverdi di Roberto D'Aversa che hanno voglia di dare conferme ai segnali incoraggianti visti col Genoa. In esclusiva per TuttoMercatoWeb, il direttore sportivo Francesco Palmieri ha scelto di presentare la sfida di domenica pomeriggio soffermandosi anche sulle insistenti voci di mercato che vedono proprio il Napoli su Sebastiano Esposito per gennaio.

"Sappiamo che sarà una partita difficilissima, il Napoli è una squadra molto molto forte. Sappiamo anche di essere in un momento complicato e in una posizione di classifica non buona, ma le squadre vanno affrontate tutte e noi siamo pronti per questa sfida", il primo pensiero del ds neroverde.

Il suo ragionamento prosegue, ancora sul Napoli: "Conosciamo il valore dell'avversario, ma noi vogliamo ricreare quelle belle cose che si sono viste nelle prime 6-7 partite di questo campionato. Dopo quelle c'è stato un momento di smarrimento, ma già nell'ultima sfida contro il Genoa ho visto segnali molto incoraggianti".

Nelle ultime ore avete perso per infortunio Adzic… "Dispiace, con Adzic e Leysen abbiamo perso due ottimi giocatori che non ci saranno per un po'. Ma abbiamo una rosa corposa e di qualità e l'allenatore saprà scegliere i giocatori giusti".

Inevitabile chiederle del mercato. A proposito di Napoli, le voci su Sebastiano Esposito si fanno sentire... "Il fatto che una squadra come il Napoli osservi i nostri giocatori fa piacere e ci inorgoglisce. Noi abbiamo puntato su Sebastiano in estate per questo ed il fatto che il suo nome sia accostato al Napoli e che sia arrivato in Nazionale dà ancora più valore alla nostra scelta. Noi adesso però dobbiamo pensare solo al nostro momento e a risollevarci in classifica".

Nessun pensiero quindi al mercato di gennaio? "In questi giorni ho letto, forse anche troppo, di queste attenzioni ma non abbiamo ricevuto chiamate. Sappiamo di avere giocatori importanti come Sebastiano, ma la nostra proprietà è forte e ha un progetto importante in mente. Storicamente a metà stagione non abbiamo mai venduto i pezzi pregiati e anche in questo caso non faremo partire nessuno".

#2099. 26-year-old steps up to prove his value in absence of influential Blackburn Rovers man: Opinion

Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford. They’ve had to deal with adversity ahead of those matches too, notably seeing head coach Tony Mowbray step back from his duties for health reasons.

Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers. Since moving to Ewood Park in the summer, the 35-year-old has emerged as a leader and formed a fine partnership with Kristi Montgomery in the middle of the park.

However, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji. After some challenging moments in his debut campaign, the 26-year-old midfielder has delivered when needed and proven his value in the Rovers squad.

Baradji joined Blackburn Rovers on an initial loan last summer, and he had to deal with injury in his first season. His impact was limited as a result, and when he was available, fans weren’t too sold on his performances.

Despite this, the Frenchman was signed permanently in the summer. When injury hit and Baradji missed the first six games of the new Championship season, many of the Rovers faithful feared a similar campaign would pan out.

However, Baradji has now played in all of the last 10 Championship games – four have come from the start, two when covering for Montgomery during his injury absence, and two while Morsy has been out. The last two appearances have been the best of the lot, battling hard to help Rovers to a point against Burnley before another well-rounded display in the mature midweek win over Watford.

Baradji has brought power in and out of possession in Morsy’s absence. He isn’t afraid to get stuck in and use his stature to muscle opponents off the ball, and his physical attributes, paired with slick footwork, make him a good ball carrier as well.

The midfielder’s per 90 stats highlight the impression he has made when called upon. As per FotMob‘s dataset, Baradji is averaging 1.30 successful dribbles per 90 (top 9% of Championship midfielders), 9.88 duels won (top 1%), 7.64 defensive contributions (top 8%) and a 75% long-ball accuracy rate (top 4%).

Baradji’s signing came with some reservations, as a deal was initially shelved when his medical raised an injury problem. However, the numbers he posted in a competitive Swiss Super League for a relegated Yverdon Sport side showed exactly why Blackburn Rovers were interested.

And, his recent performances have started to show that he can be a hit in the Championship too. Baradji pairs power and skill to offer a real force in possession, and his work rate and physicality have seen him offer the strong presence needed in the middle in Morsy’s absence.

Morsy will be backed to reclaim his place when fit. But, at 35, he isn’t a long-term option. Baradji has shown he is ready to stake a claim for a long-term spot in the Rovers team.

#2098. Chelsea join Spurs in 'monitoring' history-making France international as transfer tussle heats up

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48

Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.

Xabi Alonso is among several managers who appear to be assessing the versatile VfL Wolfsburg defender ahead of a potential transfer.

The Blues, Tottenham and Fulham are all 'monitoring' Kumbedi, while City Football Group have also been tracking his progress throughout the campaign, according to TEAMtalk.

The right-back moved to Germany from Lyon in August 2025, initially joining Wolfsburg on loan before the Bundesliga club activated their €6m purchase option.

Despite Wolfsburg suffering relegation to Bundesliga 2, Kumbedi opted to remain with the club and help them pursue an immediate return to the German top-flight.

His decision has not prevented his reputation from growing, with Zinedine Zidane handing him his first senior France call-up earlier this month following an injury withdrawal from the squad.

Kumbedi made his international debut against Italy at San Siro on November 12th, becoming the first Bundesliga 2 player to receive a France senior call-up since David Trezeguet in 2007.

Chelsea's interest in Kumbedi could make sense given the uncertainty surrounding their options at right-back.

Reece James' injury problems have created a significant headache for Alonso, with Pedro Neto having been deployed in a wing-back role and centre-back Josh Acheampong also shifted out to the right.

Malo Gusto's uncertain future at Stamford Bridge is another potential consideration, leaving Chelsea with reasons to explore the market for a specialist defender capable of providing greater depth and versatility.

European scouts are reportedly impressed by his pace, athleticism and stamina, while his ability to operate on either flank further adds to his appeal.

That versatility is particularly attractive to a side like Chelsea, who are seeking defensive reinforcements in 2027, with the French gem's performances over the coming months likely to remain under close scrutiny.

However, the west London side are not alone in their interest, with top-flight rivals Spurs, Fulham and City also monitoring the Frenchman.

His international breakthrough could make competition for his signature increasingly fierce, but Chelsea's need for greater stability and depth on the right makes this a potential transfer worth watching.

#2096. Derby County vs Watford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:49

Derby County and Watford square off at Pride Park on Saturday afternoon as two of the worst performing teams in the division.

While the Rams sit at the bottom of the Championship table, Watford are only five points ahead of them and with a head coach taking charge of his first Hornets match.

When Derby travelled to Molineux to face Wolverhampton Wanderers on Tuesday night, they would not have necessarily expected to earn anything from one of the form teams in the division.

However, despite having troubled Wolves during the opening half hour, the Rams succumbed to a 3-0 defeat and allowed their opponents to have the most shots (39) by any team in the Championship in 11 years.

John Eustace has now overseen 11 defeats in 17 league matches, and it is realistic to assume that he may be sacked if Derby lose this game.

In four of their last eight outings, Derby have conceded at least three goals, while they have only netted more than once in a fixture in 13 outings.

On a positive note, the East Midlands outfit did win their last contest at Pride Park, overcoming Bolton Wanderers by a 3-1 scoreline on November 6.

Meanwhile, Watford head into this encounter with former Romania and Legia Warsaw boss Edward Iordanescu in the dugout for his first game in English football.

The Hornets have accumulated seven points from seven matches, hardly a disaster at this stage of the season.

Nevertheless, back-to-back defeats have been posted at Sheffield United and against Blackburn Rovers without scoring a goal.

Despite holding leaders Middlesbrough to a goalless draw before the November international break, Watford have now failed to score in three successive matches.

Furthermore, they have collected just one point from eight away matches this season, that 1-1 draw at Wrexham in August being followed by seven consecutive defeats on their travels.

Oscar Fraulo and Bobby Clark are both pushing for a return to the Derby midfield.

Jack Robinson may return to the defence, whether that be as a central defender in a back three or left-back in a back four.

Eustace must decide whether to use Rhian Brewster in an unfamiliar wing-back role for the second game in a row, but Sammie Szmodics remains in a packed treatment room.

Iordanescu will be forced into at least two Watford changes through Mattie Pollock and Jordan Zemura serving suspensions.

Branimir Mlacic and Marc Bola appear likely to deputise, while Edo Kayembe, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma will also be considered for opportunities further up the pitch.

Widell-Zetterstrom; Clarke, Sanderson, Robinson; Nyambe, Ozoh, Mowatt, Clark, Brewster; Fuseini, Morris

Ravaglia; Traore, Mlacic, Coulibaly, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou, Bravo; Vata, Doumbia, Maamma

With Watford transitioning to a new head coach, it is difficult to predict how they may perform. Nevertheless, this is a must-win match for Derby and Eustace, and we are backing the Rams to net a late goal to edge this contest.

#2093. Leicester City could lose loan star in January as parent club consider recall

Leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town. Russell Martin’s side have picked up 23 points from 15 matches, winning six, drawing five and losing four.

Form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up. One of which could be loanee Harry Howell, who Brighton are considering recalling from LCFC, according to Pete O’Rourke.

Howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start. In all competitions he has two goal contributions in 13 games for the Foxes.

Brighton are considering a recall to send Howell elsewhere in January in a bid to get more game-time. A host of clubs both in England and across Europe are keen on the 18-year-old.

Howell’s loan spell at LCFC has so far failed to provide the regular senior football Brighton wanted for his development. The 18-year-old England U19 international joined the League One club in August to gain valuable first-team experience after limited opportunities at the Amex.

Martin has acknowledged Howell’s restricted role, explaining that illness disrupted his early progress. The attacking midfielder initially made a positive impression before a virus affected his fitness and forced the club to manage his minutes carefully.

By the time he returned, Leicester had established a rhythm and altered their formation, leaving Howell struggling to find a suitable place in the side.

There have been encouraging signs when given opportunities, including a league goal and promising contributions from the bench in the FA Cup. However, the overall lack of playing time means the loan has fallen short of its primary objective.

Howell was intended to be a key player for Leicester City this season but for a multitude of reasons that has not happened. With that in mind, it is no surprise that Brighton are considering moving him on.

However, that should not be a real issue for LCFC for the rest of the season. The Foxes have plenty of options in that area, with the likes of Kamari Doyle and Sammy Braybrooke currently in fine form.

Losing loanee Howell may mean that Leicester can go out and bring in another loanee in January with a squad spot opening up. With players like Conor Chaplin, Tommy Watson and Liam Cullen also in the squad, they can likely afford to bring in a play in another area instead of a direct replacement.

#2091. Gol annullato e tanti sprechi: Venezia meglio del Bologna, ma ancora 0-0 al Penzo

Segui qui la diretta testuale di Venezia-Bologna su TMW

Termina il primo tempo fra Venezia e Bologna allo stadio Penzo. Meglio i padroni di casa fino a qui, che hanno creato e sprecato almeno quattro occasioni nitide. Bologna aiutato anche dal VAR, che ha annullato il gol di Halhal dopo una lunga revisione. I rossoblu si sono resi pericolosi con un colpo di testa di Theate nella seconda parte di frazione, ma è facile intuire che Palladino proverà a scuotere i suoi dopo 45 minuti fin troppo sofferti.

Palladino lascia ancora in panchina Orsolini, fuori anche Cambiaghi: tocca a Mbangula e Bernardeschi alle spalle di Odgaard. Nicola risponde con la coppia Yeboah-Adams.

Dopo un avvio senza particolari emozioni e con tanti duelli in mezzo al campo, al 13' il primo squillo è del Venezia: Busio per Adams, per Yeboah: diagonale sul quale si esalta Skorupski in tuffo. Dagli sviluppi di un corner poco dopo arriverebbe il gol di Halhal, ma il VAR, dopo più di 5 minuti di revisione, annulla per fuorigioco di Kike Perez (a causa di un tocco di Yeboah su una palla respinta dalla difesa di Palladino.

Yeboah si mette in proprio, ma va a sbattere due volte sulla difesa rossoblu. Ancora Venezia alla mezzora: Adams pesca Kike Perez, rigore in movimento sul quale Skorupski si salva come può. La squadra di Nicola riempie bene l'area: Haps al volo manda alto un'altra buona chance. Si rivede il Bologna: Theate colpisce da ottima posizione, ma centralmente: Stankovic ferma il suo colpo di testa. Regalo di Skorupski a Yeboah, poi il portiere polacco si rifà ipnotizzando l'ecuadoriano, che spreca. Ancora 0-0 al Penzo al 45'.

#2089. West Bromwich Albion vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:09, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:54

Looking to gain ground in the race for automatic promotion, West Bromwich Albion welcome Bristol City to The Hawthorns for a Championship contest on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies are in the midst of an impressive unbeaten run in the second tier, making them the favourites with the best UK betting apps 2026 to record victory over the out-of-form Robins.

Since a 1-0 defeat by Birmingham City at The Hawthorns on October 10, West Brom have strung together an eight-game unbeaten streak (W5 D3) in the Championship, beating Bolton Wanderers last time out.

Wednesday night's match at the Toughsheet Community Stadium provided the stage for Albion's Norwegian stars to shine, with Aune Heggebo (2) and Felix Horn Myhre scoring in a 3-1 success over the Wanderers.

Now boasting the best away record in the division with 17 points collected from nine outings, James Morrison's side are back at The Hawthorns this weekend, when they will be striving for a repeat of their 3-0 battering of Millwall in the Black Country prior to the international break.

One of four Midlands clubs inside the top five of the Championship standings after 17 matches, West Brom are occupying fifth spot in the table, just three points behind pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke City.

Scoring an eye-catching eight goals across their past three league fixtures, the Baggies pose danger from an array of positions, with five different players scoring three or more Championship goals so far this term.

Following three consecutive losses at the beginning of their tricky November schedule, Bristol City stopped the rot with a respectable 1-1 draw with Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night.

It looked as if the Robins were hurtling towards their ninth defeat of the league campaign when Joe Worrall opened the scoring early on, but Cameron Pring's first goal in nearly three years secured a share of the spoils.

Winning just one of his past nine second-tier contests (D3 L5) in charge, Michael Skubala remains under severe pressure at Bristol City, who currently reside in an uninspiring 16th place in the table.

The Robins' sole victory in their current wretched run arrived on the road at Bolton on October 31, when Dom Ballard, Sam Bell and playmaker Scott Twine netted in a five-goal thriller.

Firing an attacking blank in five of their past eight matches ahead of Saturday's trip to The Hawthorns, there is no doubting that the Robins are failing to maximise the potential of Ballard and Lorent Tolaj, with the pair scoring 40 goals combined in League One last term.

After leading goalscorer Isaac Price missed the win at Bolton on Wednesday, West Brom boss Morrison revealed that the Northern Irishman is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks due to a knee injury.

The attacker joins midfielder Ousmane Diakite (calf) in the Albion treatment room, with the Mali international expected to be out until late December.

Right-back Noah Galves (knee) will not play again this season, whilst talented youngster Rabby Nzingoula is suspended for this weekend after collecting his fifth yellow card of the term at Bolton.

There was a serious injury scare for Bristol City on Tuesday night, when centre-back Luke McNally was forced off due to a knee issue.

The 27-year-old has previously missed nearly two years due to a problem with the same knee, meaning that Rob Dickie is likely to be drafted into the XI at The Hawthorns.

Sam Greenwood and Lisav Eissat were surprise omissions from the matchday squad last time out but could return to the fold on Saturday.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Campbell, Styles; Tunde, Horn Myhre, Molumby, Whitwell; Morgan, Heggebo

Collins; Tanner, Dickie, Atkinson, Pring; Wallace, Knight, Randell, Twine; Tolaj, Ballard

Aiming to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches, West Brom will be confident of beating Bristol City, even with Nzingoula, Price and Diakite all sidelined.

The Robins are certainly capable of producing a gutsy away performance but are likely to leave empty-handed on Saturday.

#2088. Birmingham City man’s impressive display offers Chris Davies a new selection headache ahead of Bolton Wanderers tie: Opinion

Birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down. BCFC won comfortably against a poor Burnley side last night to take their tally for the season to 32 points.

The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.

This was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season. A big part of the improvements on the road this term has been the defence. The Blues have conceded the fewest goals in the Championship and kept a sixth clean sheet of the season against Burnley.

On Wednesday, they did so without captain and standout centre-back Christoph Klarer due to suspension. With Dael Fry alongside Phil Neumann, Birmingham City looked just as solid at the back.

There were some questions over how the Blues would handle missing their captain against Burnley after he picked up a suspension against Stoke City. However, Dael Fry was an ideal replacement for Klarer.

Fry has struggled for game time since leaving Middlesbrough. He hadn’t started in the league up until Birmingham City’s match at Turf Moor.

The 29-year-old has had to bide his time due to Klarer and Neumann forming such a strong partnership this season, and despite this, Fry slotted into the backline perfectly. The former Boro mainstay provided the physicality and no-nonsense defending to make him an ideal partner for Neumann’s speed and ball-playing ability.

Fry was a force in both boxes as he constantly won headers in attack and defence. He won three of his five duels total and was assured in possession with 41 passes completed, seven of which were into the final third (FotMob). He showed that despite his lack of game time, he is still a top defender at the level.

BCFC were praised for signing Fry on a free in the summer due to his experience, and he looks as though he will still have an important role to play in the Blues’ promotion push this season.

Birmingham City have had to make a lot of changes this season due to injuries and suspensions. However, they have looked strong no matter who is playing.

There was a clear focus on depth in the summer window. So far, at points, Carlos Vicente, Paik Seung-ho, Max Bird, Ryan Allsop, Ethan Laird and Dael Fry have all had to come in the starting lineup to replace first-choice players this season.

Having top Championship players like coming in as backup options is a huge weapon for the Blues. Fry would be the first choice at centre-back for a lot of sides in this league.

This depth could really help Birmingham City in a promotion push this season, but it gives Davies a tough call on how best to manage Fry, as a player of his quality is sure to be eager to play more football.

Fry is a professional who can contribute away from the pitch, but his quality is clear to see, and it deserves to be on show. Davies will be more than aware of this, and he will simply encourage the player to prove he deserves to find more minutes when the chances arise.

It is harsh, but Fry likely drops out of the BCFC side for Saturday’s clash with Bolton Wanderers. Davies will have to manage the situation carefully to keep everyone happy and motivated.

#2087. Champions League, le possibilità degli azzurri: cosa serve al Napoli per i Playoff

Il pari di Manchester ha dato qualche certezza in più al Napoli e ora gli azzurri sono più vicini all’obiettivo Playoff, priorità più volte indicata dalla società e dal tecnico Massimiliano Allegri. Il Napoli ha 4 punti in classifica e con 3 gare piuttosto alla portata la sensazione è che la qualificazione ai Playoff sia ora più vicina.

Sette punti in tre partite per avere la certezza, ora non serve solo vincere in tutte le gare ma gli azzurri hanno un jolly, da giocarsi probabilmente nella sfida contro il club belga del Club Brugge.

Nelle prossime tre sfide il Napoli di Massimiliano Allegri affronterà Club Brugge e Viking in casa e gli azeri del Sabah in trasferta, tutte squadre contro il quale il Napoli parte sulla carta favorito. Gli azzurri devono arrivare almeno a 10 punti, ma possono chiudere qualsiasi discorso a quota 11 punti e quindi 7 punti almeno in tre partite.

Un pari casalingo contro il Brugge e due vittorie contro Viking e Sabah chiuderebbero il discorso e gli azzurri si garantirebbero i Playoff con la possibilità di andare agli Ottavi di finale.

#2086. Le Havre vs. Strasbourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The new manager's debut did not go to plan, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

#2084. Not a forward: Why Mikel Arteta may need to bolster surprise Arsenal position amid January twist

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier currently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

#2083. How Ayden Heaven feels about leaving Manchester United as West Ham show interest in January deal

West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window. A striker and a left-back is on the WHUFC chief’s radar, and reports have said there is an interest in Manchester United’s Ayden Heaven too.

The 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation. According to The Athletic, Heaven is keen to play more, but his true desire is to stay at Manchester United, fight for his place in the team and help their battle to rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

However, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition. Premier League clubs have made contact to gauge Heaven’s availability and there may be a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks.

Heaven started his academy career in the West Ham setup, leaving in 2019 to join Arsenal. He cemented himself as one to watch while with Arsenal, but a desire to find more first-team opportunities prompted a move to Manchester United in the winter of 2025.

He broke into the side under Ruben Amorim but has primarily played as a backup since. The London-born prospect is held in very high regard, but the need for immediate results at Manchester United means new boss Mauricio Pochettino would be taking a gamble in entrusting Heaven with a starting berth.

As a left-footed centre-back, Heaven is adept at progressing the ball from deep with a good passing ability and a willingness to carry the ball in dribbles. This aspect of his game was nurtured at Arsenal, and it has helped him slot in at Old Trafford.

He deals with aerial duels well for a player of his inexperience, but his limited senior game time has seen issues regarding anticipation and one-on-one defending arise. Heaven can develop in these scenarios over time though – he just needs regular exposure at first-team level.

A drop to the Championship could benefit Heaven. He would be backed to start regularly at West Ham, likely taking Max Kilman’s place to slot in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos at centre-back.

Playing in a team that wants to challenge for promotion and play possession football would make for good exposure for Heaven. However, it would not be a surprise if his sights are set higher.

Heaven is a highly-rated prospect who has already played Premier League football, and he will be confident in his belief that he can deliver at top-flight level if entrusted with a regular role. It could make clubs in higher leagues more attractive than WHUFC, especially on a permanent basis.

The Hammers should keep track on his situation, but be aware that they could be outdone if the door does open for Heaven to move on from Old Trafford.

Liverpool are back in action on Sunday afternoon when they square off against Everton in the Merseyside derby.

Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.

However, although they earned an impressive 3-0 win at Club Brugge in the Champions League in midweek, the Spaniard is dealing with a number of injury issues.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Everton, who are still reeling from their 4-0 defeat at Brentford last time out.

#2081. Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:55

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

“Raul came yesterday to see the doctor, the specialist, and the recuperation is going very, very well; that’s what the specialist said,” Peixoto said. “I don’t know if the medical department lets me say this, but it’s true! I think it’s not a problem.

A product of Diambars, one of the most renowned academies in Senegal, Sidy Barhama Ndiaye plays mainly on the right but can also operate on the left. While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

A 10th-placed finish in the second tier last year, just 12 months after their 111-point haul in League One, was respectable enough, but there was always the scope for more to come from Davies' squad, and they're really showing it now.

Whilst Blues look to have depth all over the pitch, one area that they could look to bolster in the upcoming January transfer window is at the top end.

He had a slow start to life in the Midlands since his £6 million move from Djurgardens in January, but August Priske has finally come alive in the Championship.

Who has the best and worst average attendances in the Championship so far this season? Football League World takes a look...

The 22-year-old Dane found the back of the net just once from his 17 Championship appearances in the second half of 2025-26, but now acclimatised to English football, he's scored seven goals in 13 outings so far in the current campaign.

Priske has forged a good understanding with Jay Stansfield in the number 10 role, but his understudies have made little impact, with German veteran Marvin Ducksch and summer recruit Luis Vazquez both failing to fire off the bench.

It leaves Davies with a dilemma ahead of January - do City let one of the pair go and bring in a new striker to battle with Priske in the second half of the season as they push for the Premier League?

Blues may do just that, as reports have been emerging about a potential striker transfer target that is based in Spain.

According to a report from Ficherío, Sevilla forward Isaac Romero is on the club's radar ahead of the window's opening at the start of 2027, with the 26-year-old Spaniard growing frustrated with life at Los Nervionenses due to a lack of game-time this season.

It's claimed that Birmingham are already in contact with the agents of Romero in regards to a deal, and that a 'significant salary' has been put on the table for him to make the move to the second tier of English football - albeit it's also reported that Romero would like to stay at Sevilla if he gets more chances of minutes.

Romero was plucked from lower league Spanish outfit Antoniano in 2019, having started his youth career with Sevilla, making his first-team debut in 2024 for the club.

Starting in just four of his 11 La Liga appearances, Romero is behind Lucas Stassin and Robbie Ure in the pecking order, but he's scored more goals than the pair put together so far in the Spanish top flight, netting three times compared to Stassin and Ure's two goals combined.

If Birmingham make good progress with a move to sign Romero from Sevilla, then it could spark a departure from St. Andrew's - but not necessarily from their striker unit.

Reports from earlier in the week claim that Sevilla have an interest in signing Blues winger Carlos Vicente, who hasn't found his best form since signing from Alaves for £7 million last January.

Vicente worked under current Sevilla boss Luis Garcia Plaza whilst he was the manager of Alaves, and he's reportedly keen to re-unite with the 27-year-old just a year after he departed for England.

Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.

Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

Chris Davies's side have already equalled the number of away victories that they managed across the entirety of last season (6) courtesy of August Priske's seventh league goal of the term and an own goal from Clarets winger Jaydon Banel at Turf Moor.

Following seven wins from their past nine second-tier contests, Birmingham are occupying fourth position in the Championship table, three points behind current pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke.

Apart from a 6-1 battering by Brentford in the EFL Cup, Blues have been impressive at St Andrew's this season, with Saturday's hosts unbeaten across their opening eight home league battles (W4 D4).

In fact, Birmingham last experienced Second City defeat in the Championship at the beginning of April, and Davies has lost just three home league games since taking charge during the summer of 2024.

Sliding towards the relegation zone, Bolton Wanderers have now won just one of their past seven Championship contests (D2 L4) after losing to West Brom at the Toughsheet Community Stadium earlier in the week.

There is no doubting that the newly-promoted side are one of the favourites to suffer relegation this season, with Steven Schumacher's troops currently six points clear of the bottom three.

Liam Millar, Jhon Solis and Jay Stansfield were rested for the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, with the trio all set to start once again this weekend.

Bolton rotated leading marksman Sam Dalby out of the starting side on Wednesday but the Englishman is fully expected to return to the XI on Saturday.

#2072. What can Mauricio Pochettino spend on January targets at Manchester United?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United spent heavily during the summer, bringing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba to Old Trafford for a combined £148million.

Despite the summer transfers, Michael Carrick failed to keep his job and was replaced by Mauricio Pochettino.

With United struggling, Pochettino is expected to bring a few new names in the January transfer window. The manager is reportedly expected to bring in no more than two players, with a new striker understood to be his biggest priority.

With the summer investment, the club is left with less flexibility as Pochettino looks to address several weaknesses in his squad.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could have less than £50million to spend in January, leaving the Argentine with limited room to spend during the winter transfer window.

According to reports from the Daily Mail, United are working within financial restrictions and are unlikely to sanction any major spending in January. The club are also mindful of the Premier League’s financial regulations, which could make it difficult to fund major names.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury problems and Joshua Zirkzee’s disappointing form have increased the need for another centre-forward.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is among the names linked with United. Pochettino already knows the United States international from their time together with the national team, which could make him an interesting option.

Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin and former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, currently playing for Al-Ahli, have also been mentioned as targets.

A left-back is another position United want to address. The club failed to bring in proper competition for Luke Shaw during the summer, despite being linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri.

However, the budget means Pochettino may have to choose his priorities carefully rather than address every problem in one window.

United recorded revenue of £677.6million despite not playing European football last season. However, the Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules restrict spending on player and head coach wages, transfer repayments and agent fees to 85 per cent of football revenue, plus net profit from player sales.

January could become a window of careful decisions for United and Pochettino but looking at their current position and form, they need far more than just 50 million. In this budget, Pochettino needs to be careful who he brings in to improve their standings.

#2070. Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

Indeed, a fresh ticketing decision made by the Owls could even promise to further boost tomorrow's attendance.

Wednesday have announced a fresh update ahead of Saturday's showdown, in which Hallam FC supporters will be able to attend free of charge.

As confirmed via the club's social media channels on Friday afternoon, Wednesday will be opening their turnstiles to fans of the Sheffield-based non-league club, who have been competing in the Northern Premier League East this term.

The offer will only be applicable to season ticket holders at Sandygate, which just happens to be world football's oldest ground. Indeed, Hallam FC are the world's second-oldest club, too, though this announcement comes upon the seventh-tier outfit's confirmation that they would be withdrawing from the seventh-tier with immediate effect following a warning that they could run out of money as early as next month.

Facing the threat of extinction owing to a "perilous" financial situation, Wednesday have extended an invitation for free attendance to all Hallam FC season ticket holders, who are able to claim their complimentary ticket in the West Stand Lower on Leppings Lane by showing their season ticket at turnstiles 14 and 17.

Other fans, however, do not feel as though Wednesday's goodwill and generosity should end there.

They're just as proud of the club's decision, but believe that even more could be done to support Hallam FC amid their crisis.

Dave Challinor can deploy Barry Bannan across the midfield, but beleives a deeper role could prolong his career at Sheffield Wednesday

One example came from this fan, who urged the League One side to put on another friendly with Hallam FC.

Perhaps more realistically, a second punter suggested providing fundraising buckets on all the turnstiles.

More specifically, many fans have taken the opportunity to hail David Storch for Wednesday's generous offering.

The Owls, of course, are no strangers to off-field crises, having endured plenty last season while encountering administration and existential threat amid a litany of missed payments to both playing and non-playing staff.

#2067. PSV Eindhoven vs. Go Ahead Eagles - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 14:12

Looking to move on from their midweek Champions League collapse against Real Madrid, PSV Eindhoven return to the bread and butter of Eredivisie football on Saturday.

The defending champions welcome Go Ahead Eagles to the Philips Stadion in gameweek 14, seeking a response to their humbling experience in the Spanish capital as they chase a fourth consecutive top-flight victory.

An Ivan Perisic goal made things interesting at the Bernabeu in midweek, but a Jude Bellingham-inspired second-half performance saw Jose Mourinho's Los Blancos run riot and eventually claim a 5-1 victory over PSV.

That loss, the Dutch giants' third in five European matches, leaves them 30th in the 36-team league-phase standings and their top-eight prospects looking increasingly remote.

However, Peter Bosz's men remain in contention for the qualification playoffs, with 24th-placed Villarreal just two points ahead of the reigning Eredivisie champions.

The Farmers will undoubtedly welcome a return to home comforts on Saturday as they seek to regain winning momentum after their chastening experience in the Spanish capital.

League football has brought greater encouragement, particularly in recent weeks, with three consecutive victories following a run of one win in four matches between late September and late October.

Scoring at least four goals in each of their victories over Willem II (7-0), Cambuur (6-2) and NEC (4-1) suggests a return to their free-scoring best, boding well for this weekend's visit from Go Ahead Eagles.

The Deventer outfit travel to Eindhoven in indifferent form, with a 1-0 away victory over SBV Excelsior coming between defeats to Cambuur and Fortuna Sittard.

Particularly notable has been the attacking decline of Joseph Oosting's men, who have scored just once across their last three league matches after averaging 2.3 goals per game over the opening 10 gameweeks.

While that sample remains too small for firm conclusions, the Pride of the IJssel's dip cannot be dismissed ahead of their trip to the Philips Stadion, where Kowet claimed a stunning 2-1 KNVB Beker semi-final victory in February 2025 en route to lifting their first domestic cup.

Paul Simonis was in charge for that historic success as Go Ahead Eagles secured their first victory in Eindhoven for 57 years, and they now seek a first Eredivisie win at PSV since 1968.

That will be easier said than done, however, as their historical struggles and recent scoring decline leave them vulnerable against hosts still reeling from their Santiago Bernabeu beatdown.

Mauro Junior (groin), Sami Ouaissa (muscle), Adamo Nagalo, Alassane Plea and Jerdy Schouten (ACL) remain unavailable for PSV; however, Ricardo Pepi should feature in some capacity after remaining on the bench in Madrid.

No player has scored more Eredivisie goals than Sven Mijnans, with the versatile attacking midfielder registering nine strikes and three assists in the top flight.

Guus Til is likely to lead the attack despite Pepi's availability, while Ruben van Bommel offers a dual threat after contributing five goals and three assists.

Soren Tengstedt shares Mijnans's position atop the league's scoring charts, with no player outscoring the Kowet forward this season.

Stefan Ingi Sigurdarson (four goals, one assist) and Mathis Suray (three goals, four assists) also possess match-winning quality that Oosting will hope comes to the fore at the Philips Stadion.

Go Ahead Eagles remain without Pim Saathof (ACL), while Evert Linthorst and Dean James will be assessed closer to kick-off.

Kovar; Dest, Geertruida, Obispo, Kostic; Sano, Fernandez; Perisic, Mijnans, Van Bommel; Til

Cillessen; Sampsted, Dirksen, Kramer, Baeten; Meulensteen, Rahmouni; Tengstedt, Edvardsen, Suray; Sigurdarson

#2066. ‘Not Manchester United standard’, Paul Merson raises concerns over Manchester United squad

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have failed to hit the numbers expected off them after a lackluster campaign so far.

Michael Carrick was relieved off his duties after winning just 1 game in his first 10, while collecting only 8 points. Manchester United arr currently languishing in the relegation spots and Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, has a massive task ahead.

Manchester United have been leaky in defence and haven’t gone a game without conceding a goal this season. Their attacking returns are equally disappointing with United failing to convert chances regularly.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson said.

However, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

“I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”

“And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

#2065. Exclusive: Fresh Robbie Fowler to Swindon Town update revealed after Ian Holloway sack

Swindon Town are on the search for a new manager, with Ian Holloway's time at the County Ground coming to an end earlier in the week.

The 63-year-old had been in charge of the Robins for the past two years, having endured a storied career which has taken him to the Premier League with both Blackpool and Crystal Palace.

Improvement was showed in both seasons finished by Holloway, with 12th and ninth-placed finishes in League Two, but results have been indifferent during the current campaign, with back-to-back defeats over Grimsby Town and Newport County leading to his dismissal.

Swindon's hierarchy - which includes chairman Clem Morfuni - must now find Holloway's successor, and FLW can exclusively reveal that one individual who is on the radar is none other than Premier League legend Robbie Fowler.

Fowler scored 163 Premier League goals in his career for Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City, whilst also appearing 26 times for the England national team, before winding down his career in Australia and Thailand.

We looked at five potential replacements Swindon Town should consider if they part company with under-pressure manager Ian Holloway.

Since his retirement, Fowler has been well-travelled as a manager, with spells in both Thailand and Australia, as well as India and Saudi Arabia, but he's yet to land a job in his native England, having been without a role since being with Al-Qadsiah in 2023.

That could now change though, with Football League World understanding that the 51-year-old is a live contender to become the latest person to have a go at the Town job.

One of the reasons that Fowler is being admired by Swindon chairman Morfuni is his time in his native Australia, FLW can reveal.

After a spell at Blackburn Rovers, Fowler moved down under in 2009 to play for North Queensland Fury, a stint which lasted a year before moving on to fellow Aussie club Perth Glory.

Fowler would join Muangthong United in Thailand in 2011 and end up becoming their player-manager for a short period of time, but some eight years after leaving Australia, the former striker would return as a manager, taking the Brisbane Roar job.

Managing 23 games for the Queensland-based outfit, Fowler won 11 times as their manager, before the A-League was suspended in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic - he wouldn't return to the club as he relocated to be closer to his family.

A further 20 matches were managed for East Bengal between 2020 and 2021, before a stint in Saudi with Al-Qadsiah lasted just three months, despite winning six of his eight matches in charge and going unbeaten in the Saudi second tier, with the club wanting to move to a more Spanish-style model, according to Fowler himself.

#2062. Real Madrid vs. Alaves: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:18

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday evening.

Los Blancos will enter the league fixture off the back of a thumping 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side have now won each of their last 10 matches in all competitions, including their last six fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 in the league last time out, and they currently sit second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona.

Alaves, meanwhile, have been one of the success stories in La Liga this season, picking up 16 points from 13 matches, which has left them in ninth spot in the table.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the head-to-head record and looks at the previous meetings between the two teams ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital.

Real Madrid have tackled Alaves on 46 occasions throughout history, and unsurprisingly, the Madrid giants lead the overall head-to-head record with 38 wins to Alaves five, while there have only ever been three draws between the two teams.

Karim Benzema is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored nine times against Alaves during his time at Real Madrid.

Real Madrid are on 121 goals against Alaves, conceding just 34, and Los Blancos are on a nine-game winning run against the Basque side.

That said, Alaves do have a recent famous win over Real Madrid to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory when the two teams locked horns at Bernabeu in November 2020, thanks to goals from Lucas Perez and Joselu.

Alaves have beaten Real Madrid only twice since 2000, though, while there has not been a draw between the two sides since October 2001.

Two of Alaves' five wins over Los Blancos have actually come at the Bernabeu, also triumphing 1-0 in the famous stadium back in 2000.

In La Liga, the teams have met on 40 occasions, with Real Madrid winning 34 times to Alaves' four, drawing twice in the process.

Apr 21, 2026: Real Madrid 2-1 Alaves (La Liga)

Dec 14, 2025: Alaves 1-2 Real Madrid (La Liga)

Apr 13, 2025: Alaves 0-1 Real Madrid (La Liga)

Sept 24, 2024: Real Madrid 3-2 Alaves (La Liga)

#2061. Dave Challinor sends Sheffield Wednesday message after Barry Bannan captaincy query

Sheffield Wednesday's captaincy situation has been played down by Dave Challinor, despite Barry Bannan handing the armband to Liam Cooper and not Liam Palmer in last Friday night's win at Barnsley.

Henrik Pedersen installed Palmer as the club captain in January when Bannan left Hillsborough to join Millwall. After returning to Sheffield Wednesday in the summer, Bannan didn't pick up the armband he left behind, with Palmer instead continuing in the role.

However, the defender has been in just three starting line-ups this season, meaning Bannan has taken over the armband a considerable amount of the time under both Pedersen and Challinor.

In last Friday's win against Barnsley at Oakwell, Bannan wore the armband until he was replaced by Harry Gray in the 78th minute. Despite Palmer coming off the bench seven minutes earlier, it was Cooper who took the armband.

In the wake of that happening, Challinor was quizzed by Joe Crann of The Wednesday Word about the captaincy situation.

He responded by confirming he'd not given who wore the armband at Oakwell much thought at all.

"I've given it zero thought," he said. "Baz came off and whoever he passes the armband to (is the captain). I've said before, I'm not huge on — I know some of them (the players and fans) will be — who wears the armband."

Challinor also offered an insight into his leadership group: "We have a group that I spoke to on the first day I came into the building — the leadership group. Baz, Palms (Palmer), Coops (Cooper), Lummers (Joe Lumley), Billy (Mitchell) and Dish (Di-Shon Bernard) are all part of that. It makes no odds, I want leaders on the pitch.

"If you're wearing an armband, it makes no difference to me."

Wednesday are back in action on Saturday afternoon when they host Reading FC at Hillsborough.

Who should be Sheffield Wednesday captain? Let us know in the comments!

Pedersen was in a difficult position when Bannan walked out of Hillsborough to go to Millwall, and the obvious choice was to give the captaincy to Palmer — a long-standing member of the squad and someone who had stuck with Wednesday through difficult periods.

Bannan's return to the club in the summer led to many believing he would take on the captaincy again, but Pedersen rightly stuck by the man who had stuck by Wednesday in Palmer.

The fact Palmer isn't a guaranteed starter makes this a topic of discussion once again. If Bannan is starting the majority of games and Palmer isn't, he will naturally wear the armband more. The same can be said of Cooper, who has started 13 times in the league this season. He was the club captain at Leeds United for a decade and led them to the Premier League — he's another strong candidate to captain Wednesday.

A new manager also brings new ideas, and Challinor won't have the loyalty to Palmer that Pedersen did. He's also clearly got a few contenders in Lumley, Mitchell and Bernard, who could be longer-term options for the captaincy.

A change in the coming months would be no surprise.
