#2060. Manchester United ready to part ways with Lisandro Martinez despite defensive issues

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United are reportedly leaning towards allowing Lisandro Martinez to leave next summer, with the club increasingly doubtful about extending the defender’s contract beyond the current season.

According to GIVEMESPORT journalist Ben Jacobs, Manchester United are not expected to activate the one-year extension included in Martinez’s deal. The Argentine’s contract expires next summer, although the club retain the option to keep him until 2028.

The situation is surprising given United’s ongoing problems at the back. They have struggled to find consistency in defence, with Matthijs de Ligt still working towards full match sharpness, Leny Yoro continuing his development and Harry Maguire struggling for regular opportunities. In the latest development, Ayden Heaven is also leaning towards going on a loan to secure regular minutes as he finds limited opportunities at United.

The 28-year-old arrived from Ajax in 2022 for an initial £56.7 million but has suffered two serious ACL injuries during his time at Old Trafford. His performances have also come under scrutiny this season, adding further uncertainty to his future.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs suggested that Manchester United are already considering a defensive rebuild ahead of next summer.

“I think the Lisandro Martinez direction of travel is a departure, and there is the option to extend by one year. But my gut says that Manchester United, even if they can’t get defenders in the winter, will add further in the summer,” Jacobs said.

Jacobs also suggested that activating Martinez’s extension would not necessarily mean the club intend to keep him.

“Even if Man United extend the contract, that might just be a protection so they can still sell him,” he added.

Although the decision is not yet final but Manchester United are leaning towards letting Martinez go. They find themselves in a difficult place as far as their defensive cover is concerned. Despite their shortage of reliable defenders, the club appears increasingly open to moving on from the Argentine.

#2059. Torino vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23

Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.

Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, Lazio sit three points above reigning champions Inter and two clear of city rivals Roma after storming through their first dozen games.

Having begun Gennaro Gattuso's reign with a shock Coppa Italia loss to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have since gone up through the gears, only dropping four points in Serie A so far.

Victory this week would take them onto 11 wins from 13 games, and the last team to make such a fast start was Napoli in the 2022-23 campaign, when they ultimately went on to win the title.

Lazio's most recent success, against Lecce, featured goals from two of their star players this term, as Tijjani Noslin bagged a brace before Davide Frattesi capped things off with a cheeky chip from outside the box.

Ahead of next month's Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could well be at stake, fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

However, Gattuso will not look any further than Saturday's trip north to Turin, where Lazio have won half of their last 22 Serie A games against Torino.

That said, the capital club did not prevail when they last met in March, as Torino won 2-0 at Stadio Olimpico Grande.

So, the hosts can now seek back-to-back victories over Lazio for the first time since 2013, even if current form suggests they may fail.

While their Roman rivals are flying high, Toro have endured an uneven season under new boss Ignazio Abate: following a slow start, they then posted three consecutive wins, before slipping back down the table.

After last week's 1-0 loss to Napoli, Abate's side have picked up just one point from their last four matches, leaving them closer to the drop zone than Italy's top six.

While leaving Naples with anything is always a tough task, they cannot expect to thrive when they return to Turin.

Not only have the Granata conceded an average of nearly two goals per game there this season, but they are also on a record run of 11 Serie A home games without a clean sheet.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has generally stuck to a similar Lazio lineup, but he is currently missing two regular starters.

Though defensive duo Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo are both sidelined with flexor injuries, captain Mattia Zaccagni has resumed full training and could be named on the bench.

While Frattesi is the visitors' top scorer with five Serie A goals, Noslin has notched at least one goal involvement in all of his last four matches.

Torino have been less potent this term, but Che Adams has four top-flight strikes and Giovanni Simeone must love playing his father's old club - the Argentinian has previously scored 10 league goals against Lazio.

Ardian Ismajli limped out of the loss to Napoli with an adductor injury and has subsequently undergone surgery, while Abate has fitness doubts about wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez.

As Belghali is still suffering with knee inflammation, Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could fill in on the hosts' right flank.

Perri; Comuzzo, Coco, Comert; Aboukhlal, Braganca, Mandragora, Vlasic, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Well acquainted from their Milan days, Gattuso and Abate will be foes for 90 minutes this weekend, when Lazio should continue their long unbeaten run.

As Torino struggle to keep clean sheets, the league leaders are sure to score, and they have conceded under one goal per game so far this term.

#2058. West Ham must muscle in on Celtic transfer target to solve major Scott Parker headache

West Ham have had a very poor season so far in the Championship, with the Hammers way off the pace for a top two finish.

Not only did many observers expect the Hammers to bounce back to the Premier League at the first attempt, but they were widely tipped to win the league.

Therefore, the fact they are in the bottom half after 17 games, and some 11 points away from second-place is a massive underachievement.

Nuno Espírito Santo paid the price for an inconsistent start by losing his job at the start of the month, but the decision to appoint Scott Parker hasn’t paid off just yet, as the former player is without a win in four.

However, with Parker having won promotion from the Championship with three different clubs, there’s no doubting his CV at this level. So, his early struggles have opened up a wider discussion on why West Ham are failing, and the players are coming under scrutiny.

In truth, you could identify several areas of the pitch that need addressing, but there’s no doubt that the goalkeeper position is giving Parker a major headache at the moment.

Mads Hermansen started as his number one, but the Dane has had a terrible time of things since he moved to the Londoners, and he was taken out of the firing line after a poor performance at Blackburn a few weeks ago.

With Alphonse Areola injured, youngster Fin Herrick has had the gloves for the past two games, but he didn’t convince for Preston’s opener last Saturday, and he made a mistake in the 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth on Tuesday.

So, it remains to be seen who starts against Stoke, with Areola likely to play if he is available. Yet, even if he is, the Frenchman hasn’t exactly played well for West Ham for a long time now, and there are doubts over both his fitness and mentality.

Therefore, bringing in a new number one could quickly become a priority for Parker as soon as the window opens in January, and Blackburn’s Balazs Toth is someone who should be on their radar.

The Hungarian was heavily linked with Celtic in the summer transfer window, but Rovers managed to keep him at Ewood Park, although he's still thought to be a target for the Glasgow giants.

Toth has shown why he was so highly regarded after producing some big saves for Blackburn this season, although he perhaps hasn’t got back to the heights he had set in the previous campaign.

Unfortunately for Blackburn and Toth, he is currently out with a hand injury sufered on international duty with Hungary that could sideline him until mid-January, but he has done enough over the years to earn a reputation as a reliable Championship keeper.

Due to his injury, it’s no exaggeration to say there’s a possibility that Toth has played his last game for Blackburn, as there are major doubts over his future going into the New Year.

That’s because Toth’s contract is expiring in the summer of 2027, so, unless fresh terms are agreed, then this will be the last window for Rovers to get a fee for the 29-year-old.

Which of the division's shot-stoppers would likely be the costliest in the transfer market? FLW takes a look...

It has been claimed previously that Toth is not keen on signing an extension, so that will put clubs on alert going into January.

Whether Blackburn are willing to sanction a sale when they have a chance to make the play-offs remains to be seen, but it would certainly make financial sense to avoid letting an asset go for nothing.

From West Ham’s perspective, Toth’s contract means he is a very realistic target in what could be a challenging month for the club.

If West Ham remain off the pace in terms of pushing for the top two, selling clubs will know that the Irons are desperate.

We saw last January how the club spent big on the likes of Taty Castellanos and Pablo, and the latter in particular has proven to be a disastrous signing.

Which position must West Ham prioritise in the January window? Let us know in the comments below.

So, the club won’t want to waste more money in the winter window, and they also need players who are capable of making an instant impact at the London Stadium, as there will be no period to allow them to settle in.

That makes Toth an attractive option due to his experience at this level, and he should be fit in time for the home game against Swansea on January 15 if a deal is agreed.

#2057. Man Utd make four changes as Pochettino names starting XI for Sporting clash

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have confirmed their starting lineup for Wednesday night’s Champions League meeting with Sporting Lisbon, with Mauricio Pochettino making changes after Sunday’s heavy defeat to Liverpool.

The Red Devils travel to Portugal looking to respond after a difficult start to life under their new head coach. Manchester United were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Pochettino’s first match in charge, with Leny Yoro sent off inside the opening eight minutes.

Yoro’s dismissal disrupted United’s plans but the defender is available for tonight as his suspension only applies to domestic football.

Pochettino has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation for the trip to Lisbon, with Senne Lammens starting in goal. Noussair Mazraoui, Harry Maguire, Yoro and Lisandro Martinez make up the defensive line.

Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans start in midfield, while Amad, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are named upfront behind Joshua Zirkzee, who gets his start this season.

United have several players unavailable or struggling with fitness issues ahead of the game. Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte remain sidelined with longer-term problems, while Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford are also dealing with issues.

Matheus Cunha is another absentee. The forward is suspended for the game after seeing a red against AS Roma.

Those absences have limited Pochettino’s options as he looks to find a response in his second match at the helm.

United face a difficult test against a Sporting side that have gone nine matches without defeat. The Portuguese side have no major injury concerns, with all key players available.

The pressure is already building on Pochettino after the defeat at Anfield. A positive result in Lisbon would offer United a chance to put that disappointment behind them, but they will need a far more disciplined performance to get anything from the game.

#2056. Mauricio Pochettino proud of Man Utd response after chaotic Sporting draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino praised Manchester United’s character and spirit after his side earned a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Manchester United travelled to Portugal looking to respond after their disappointing 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge. They showed a much-improved performance away from home, although a number of costly moments prevented the new head coach from celebrating his first victory.

Bruno Fernandes scored twice on his return to the stadium, putting United ahead after Luis Suarez had given Sporting the lead. The home striker also scored twice, including a penalty, to ensure the points were shared.

Senne Lammens had earlier saved a Suarez spot-kick, but the United goalkeeper was involved in another penalty incident that allowed the Sporting forward to find the net. United also had two goals ruled out, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late in the contest.

Despite the frustrating outcome, Pochettino was pleased with what he saw from his players.

The Argentine felt United controlled large periods of the first half but were disappointed to go into the break behind.

“The first half I think we controlled the game, I think we dominated. We were disappointed to finish the first half 1-0 down,” Pochettino said after the game.

“The second half I think we started the way we want to play. That is the style, the character. That is the way we want to establish and feeling this way we can perform.”

The United boss also made it clear that he was proud of the players despite the decisions and incidents that went against them.

“I’m so proud of my players. I think it was a very tough game. I liked the team during 90 minutes, in the way that we showed personality and character.”

Pochettino felt his side had been punished repeatedly in important moments.

“In the second half, we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half. We were aggressive and I think that is the way we want to play,” he added.

After the heavy defeat at Anfield, United showed a different level of fight in Lisbon. The draw will still feel like a missed opportunity for Manchester United and Pochettino. However, the Argentine manager believes his players are beginning to embrace the style of play he wants.

#2055. Birmingham City urged to 'say no' to ex-Celtic star and eye Leeds United, Ipswich Town transfers

Birmingham City are in the chase for a place in the Premier League, but one of the players they've been connected with for the January transfer window is giving FLW's Birmingham correspondent doubts.

Following a disappointing 1-0 reversal at Stoke City last weekend, Birmingham City got themselves back on track with a 2-0 win at struggling Burnley on Tuesday night. The Blues are in fourth place in the Championship, and the race for a coveted place in the Premier League is looking extremely tight, with just three points separating the top five sides in the division.

The January transfer window offers a final opportunity to tweak squads for the second half of the season, but this could mean departures as well as arrivals, and one player who's been linked with a move away from St Andrew's in the new year is winger Carlos Vicente, who's been reported to be of interest to the Spanish club Sevilla.

In the event that this should come to pass, Birmingham will have a gap to fill in that position, and one name who has been put forward is that of the Israeli international Liel Abada, who's currently playing in MLS for Charlotte FC. With a place in the Premier League worth a minimum of £200 million potentially at stake, it's an important window for the Blues.

The decisions to be made in the January transfer window could be highly consequential for Birmingham City, so Football League World have been in contact with our Blues fan pundit Jason Moore for his assessment over a potential replacement for Carlos Vicente.

Jason has doubts over whether Abada is the right man for the job: "If that's the replacement for Vicente, I'd say no. He played in the Scottish league but how many players from the Scottish league are really good nowadays? We got Furuhashi, who played in that league, and he was absolutely shocking for us."

Who would you pick as a replacement for Carlos Vicente if Birmingham lose him in January? Let us know in the comments below!

Jason feels that Birmingham can do better than Abada, if they do have to part ways with Vicente: "I don't think the Scottish league is quite up to scratch any more. In the nicest way, he's playing out in MLS and while there are some good players in MLS, I think for the calibre of player we're looking at, I'd rather we were looking elsewhere. If we were going to lose Vicente, I'd be wanting something a bit better."

But there is one Championship player who Jason believes could be a good replacement for Vicente, and he wants his club to show some ambition in the January window: "For me, I'd want to get an out and out winger who's pure pace but has got a bit more of a pedigree. I wouldn't mind getting Ramazani from Burnley, get him off Leeds permanently, because I think there's a player there, I think he looks really good, and then get Mehmeti as well; make a real statement in January if we're still there or thereabouts near the top of the league, just go for it. And if we lose Vicente, I'd love someone like Ramazani."

Birmingham City have reignited their interest in former Celtic winger Liel Abada to join Wolves in the race for his signature this winter

With 16 appearances so far in 2026-27, of which 10 have been starts, Carlos Vicente has been an integral part of the Birmingham City squad this season, and the appeal of a move to La Liga for a Spanish player is extremely clear.

Should Sevilla make their move and Vicente be open to it, a space will open up in the Blues first-team squad which needs filling before the end of the month, and Liel Abada's numbers are strong. He's a regular in the Charlotte FC team, and has made 28 appearances for them so far throughout their 2026 season, of which 20 have been starts, and he has scored 11 goals and contributed five assists.

But while the former Spurs manager Ange Postecoglou once described Abada as "outstanding", the winger has no experience of playing in the English leagues. And this may make Largie Ramazani of interest to them. Ramazani has been one of the few bright spots of a dismal first half of the season on loan at Burnley from Leeds United, with five goals and one assist in 14 appearances for the Clarets so far in 2026-27. He started his career in the Manchester United academy and also made 31 appearances, scoring seven goals, for Leeds United in their promotion-winning 2024-25 season.

The upcoming January transfer window is likely to be an extremely busy, given that there remain so many clubs who, with a good run of results, put themselves in contention for a place in the Premier League. With the limitless ambition of the club's owners and it having been 16 years since they were last there, Birmingham City have a huge opportunity this season, but this makes it crucial that they get their decisions right in the new year.

#2054. Rangers vs Falkirk - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 14:21

The Scottish Premiership's second and third-placed sides will meet on Saturday, when Rangers welcome Falkirk to Ibrox Stadium.

The hosts are second in the Scottish Premiership standings with 33 points, one point behind leaders Celtic, while the visitors are third with 24 points from 14 matches.

Rangers head into Saturday's match with their sights set on moving to the top of the Scottish Premiership standings for the first time this season.

The Gers trail leaders Celtic by just one point, meaning a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals, at least until the Bhoys take on Hearts on Sunday afternoon.

Derek McInnes' men will be full of confidence of claiming all three points, with Rangers heading into the matchday 15 fixture enjoying a sensational 14-game unbeaten run across all competitions.

In the league, Rangers have won 10 and drawn two matches during that run, including winning each of their last three Scottish Premiership fixtures, beating St Mirren 2-0, Motherwell 2-1 and Aberdeen 3-2.

The Gers are also looking to extend their superb record at Ibrox, having won all of their last nine home games, scoring 22 and conceding just four goals in that time.

Despite their fantastic form coming into this match, Rangers will expect a tough test against visitors Falkirk, who travel to Ibrox off the back of six consecutive league triumphs.

That run includes particularly notable wins against Celtic (2-0) and Hearts (5-2), and the Bairns will now be looking to add Rangers' scalp to their collection.

Thanks to those six victories, Falkirk have rapidly ascended to third in the Scottish Premiership standings with 24 points from 14 matches, although they only lead Hearts - who have played one game fewer - by one point.

Alongside their impressive recent run, Falkirk will draw further self belief from their formidable record on the road this season, recording three wins, three draws and suffering just one loss away from home in the league.

John McGlynn's side have, however, failed to defeat Rangers in any of their last seven encounters, including a 2-1 defeat earlier this season.

Rangers are set to be without Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti due to ongoing injuries, while Ross McCrorie is also a doubt with a hamstring injury.

Ryan Don Naderi is Rangers' top scorer in the league with seven goals, and the forward should continue just behind Kevin Kelsy in the forward line.

Falkirk are also contending with several injury absences, including Aidan Nesbitt, Aodhan Doherty, Brad Spencer, Leon McCann and Ryan Strain, while Ethan Laidlaw is a doubt to feature.

Jacob Murrell is Falkirk's top scorer with eight league goals, including seven in his last seven appearances, and the forward will start just ahead of Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames in attack.

Both teams head into this match in fantastic form, leading us to expect a hard-fought encounter. However, given Rangers' formidable Ibrox form and their recent upperhand in this fixture, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

#2053. Pochettino fumes at ‘impossible’ decisions after Man Utd draw with Sporting

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated by several refereeing decisions during Manchester United’s 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon, insisting his side were punished in key moments of the game.

Manchester United had to settle for a point in Portugal after a chaotic evening away from home. Bruno Fernandes scored twice, but Luis Suarez also found the net on two occasions to deny Pochettino his first win as United head coach.

Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions. He ruled out an Amad Diallo goal after penalising Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, blowing his whistle before the ball crossed the line. That meant VAR could not intervene on the goal and it was not given.

The Polish official also awarded Sporting a first-half penalty and disallowed what would have been a late United winner. He blew whistle on Patrick Dorgu for pushing goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, disallowing the goal.

Pochettino did not hide his frustration when asked about the decisions after the match.

“I think your first question is difficult to answer because I think everyone knows all that was, it was impossible,” he said after the game.

“You know, it’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field. It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions.”

United also conceded an 80th-minute equaliser after Senne Lammens failed to hold a cross, allowing Suarez to score from close range.

However, Pochettino was keen to defend his goalkeeper rather than blame him for the mistake.

“I think, please, it’s to blame us,” the United boss said.

He acknowledged that his side needed to manage such situations better.

“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve, you know, the small details that for sure we will improve.”

Pochettino’s frustration was understandable after two similar incidents of bad refereeing in his first two games at United. Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was later overturned on appeal, while a series of errors against Sporting cost him yet another victory. But despite the errors, Pochettino also recognises that his players need to improve their decision-making during games.

#2052. Bruno Fernandes tells players what to do next after Sporting draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes has urged Manchester United to stick together and fight for their season after they were held to a 2-2 draw by Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The United captain scored twice on his return to the stadium, putting Manchester United ahead after Luis Suarez had given Sporting the lead. The home striker also scored twice, including a penalty, to ensure the points were shared.

Senne Lammens had earlier saved a Suarez spot-kick, but the United goalkeeper was involved in another penalty incident that allowed the Sporting forward to find the net. United also had two goals ruled out after some controversial decisions, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late in the contest.

It was another frustrating result for United, who are still searching for their first win under Mauricio Pochettino. Fernandes believes there were positives in the performance, but insists the team must now focus on getting results.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Fernandes revealed that Pochettino wanted his players to show more aggression after the break.

“[At half-time the manager] wanted more aggression. more bodies. The first goal comes from that.”

The Portuguese midfielder felt United had controlled much of the first half despite conceding. He admitted they needed more presence in the final third.

“Obviously, I think we started the game well. We gave a penalty away where Senne [Lammens] saved it. We gave one or two counters, but we were very good in recovery positions.

“They got the goal, but we were still in control of the game. We didn’t have much people in the last third. Second half we got the two goals. That was the moment we should push a bit more.”

United’s inability to hold on to their lead was another setback, but Fernandes refused to single out individuals for the mistakes.

“Mistakes are part of football and from that you get goals. Everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and we do bad as well. We need to be together in the good and in the bad moments.”

“We need points to get through. and we need to focus on the next one. Now the moment is to get back to the Premier League. We need to stick together and fight for our lives.”

#2051. Lincoln City warned against repeating Michael Skubala 'experiment' with Gavin Strachan

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a new head coach after parting company with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw earlier this week.

Lincoln won the League One title last season to secure a return to the second tier of English football for the first time in 65 years, but just weeks after sealing promotion, they lost head coach Michael Skubala to Bristol City, with Cohen and Shaw stepping up to replace him.

It is fair to say that Lincoln's decision to appoint Cohen and Shaw as joint-head coaches raised a few eyebrows, and they were widely tipped for relegation at the start of the season, but the pair made an impressive start to life in the Sincil Bank dugout.

After losing their opening two games, the Imps went on a five-game unbeaten run which lifted them to as high as eighth in the Championship table in mid-September, but results have declined significantly in recent months.

Lincoln have won just one of their last 10 games, and after suffering their fifth consecutive defeat as they were hammered 4-0 at Charlton Athletic on Tuesday night, Cohen and Shaw were dismissed on Wednesday morning with the club sitting 21st, just three points clear of the relegation zone.

There has been a shortage of rumours about potential successors to Cohen and Shaw so far, but journalist Alan Nixon reported on Thursday that West Bromwich Albion coach Gavin Strachan is one name under consideration by the Imps.

Strachan has plenty of coaching experience under his belt, having previously worked at the likes of Peterborough United, Doncaster Rovers and Celtic, and he has been part of James Morrison's backroom staff at The Hawthorns since the summer, but his only managerial experience is a brief four-and-a-half month spell with seventh tier side Ilkeston in 2015.

When asked for his thoughts on the possible appointment of Strachan, FLW's Lincoln City fan pundit Gary Hutchinson insisted that the Imps cannot afford to take a risk like they did with Skubala in League One, and he urged the club to bring in a manager with Championship experience.

"I think Gavin Strachan would be too much of a gamble for the club," Gary told FLW.

"I think they're looking for somebody with managerial experience.

"We're not in the same position as when we appointed Michael Skubala.

"When we were in League One, even though we were a smaller fish, there were always six or seven teams below us with smaller budgets, so we were expected not to be in the bottom four.

"The bottom four was failure, so we could afford to experiment a little bit, and that was the case with Michael Skubala.

"I think this calls for the same sort of thing as we had in the National League, get a manager in who understands the division a little bit more and who perhaps has experience of handling players and picking players up because they're going to need that.

"That performance on Tuesday night was not good enough.

"Whilst Gavin Strachan may well be a very good coach, we've had two coaches at the helm, and I think we need somebody who's got experience of the top job, as well as the coaching credentials.

"Bear in mind, on the coaching field, we've got Paul McShane and Shaun Pearson, who are both very competent coaches, so we need a figurehead to pull that back in.

"I just think, with Gavin Strachan, his lack of actual managerial experience will hold him back."

Who has the best and worst average attendances in the Championship so far this season? Football League World takes a look...

Lincoln have often taken gambles with their managerial decisions over the years, and they were certainly rewarded for the bold appointment of Skubala, whose only senior dugout experience prior to his arrival at Sincil Bank was a few games as caretaker of Leeds United in the Premier League.

However, the failed Cohen and Shaw experiment underlines the dangers of such risks in the Championship, and while the duo's time in charge should not be remembered as a disaster given that the Imps are currently outside the relegation zone, they should learn lessons and make a safer choice on this occasion.

Who should Lincoln City target to replace Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw? Tell us in the comments below!

Strachan is clearly a talented coach who has enjoyed plenty of success during his career, including helping Celtic to five consecutive Scottish Premiership titles, and he has made a big impact at West Brom this season, but he would not be the right man for Lincoln at this time.

#2050. Real Madrid vs Alaves - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.

Real Madrid will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League, with that success making it 10 victories in a row in all competitions.

Jose Mourinho's side are flying, with their winning run including six in Spain's top flight, and they are currently second in the La Liga table, only three points off the leaders Barcelona.

Los Blancos now have three straight league matches against Alaves, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao before resuming their Champions League campaign away to Arsenal on December 9.

Real Madrid would go level on points with Barcelona should they manage to win this match, and they have been victorious in 38 of their previous 46 games against Alaves in all competitions, suffering only five defeats in the process.

Vinicius Junior is still finding it difficult to show his best form for Real Madrid, but Kylian Mbappe is having another incredible campaign, netting 19 times in 18 appearances in all competitions.

Alaves will be the huge underdogs this weekend, but two of their last three wins over Real Madrid have come away from home, including a 2-1 success at Bernabeu in November 2020.

The Blue and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Deportivo La Coruna, with the result leaving them in ninth spot in the La Liga table on 16 points, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats from their 13 matches.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have been excellent at home this season, picking up 13 points from seven matches, but they are still waiting for their first away success of the campaign.

Alaves finished 14th in Spain's top flight last season, only one point above the relegation zone, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27.

The Basque outfit will be the fresher of the two teams following Real Madrid's Champions League involvement, but they will be up against a side that have the second-best defensive record (11 conceded) and second-best attacking record (33 scored) during the current season.

Real Madrid will be missing Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg), Ferland Mendy (hip) and Endrick (groin) through injury on Saturday, but no fresh issues have been reported.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSV, with Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen potentially all being introduced into the defence.

Jude Bellingham should also return to the starting side, with Yan Diomande potentially being rested from the first whistle to allow Arda Guler and Vinicius Junior to feature in the wide areas.

As for Alaves, Facundo Garces (knee), Mikel Rodriguez (knee) and Hugo Noava (muscle) are unavailable.

Given the nature of the result and indeed the performance against Deportivo last time out, it is possible that it could be same again in terms of the starting team for the visitors.

Lucas Boye has scored six times in 12 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set to feature in the final third, while Denis Suarez and Antonio Blanco are also set to be in the XI.

Alaves deserve credit for what has been a solid season to date, but Real Madrid are in a good place at the moment, and we are fully expecting Mourinho's side to claim another three points.

#2049. Ashley Young tears into referee after Manchester United denied dramatic late winner

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United had to settle for a point in Portugal after a chaotic evening away from home.

Bruno Fernandes scored twice, but Luis Suarez also found the net on two occasions to deny Pochettino his first win as United head coach.

Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions. He ruled out an Amad Diallo goal after penalising Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, blowing his whistle before the ball crossed the line. That meant VAR could not intervene on the goal and it was not given.

The Polish official also awarded Sporting a first-half penalty and disallowed what would have been a late United winner. He blew whistle on Patrick Dorgu for pushing goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, disallowing the goal.

The decisions left plenty of frustration among Manchester United supporters, but former footballer Ashley Young called the officiating disgraceful.

Young questioned several decisions made by Marciniak, particularly the disallowed Amad goal and the late incident involving Dorgu.

“The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave, including the one for what should have been Amad’s equaliser, with Tielemans, were unbelievable,” Ashley Young said while talking to BBC.

“Tielemans getting booked, which should never have been a booking, and then eventually getting sent off later. It should have been an equalising goal.

“Then the third goal as well, which should have stood, because he’s saying there’s a foul, whether he’s saying Lisandro Martinez or Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he’s even touched.

“How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”

The disallowed goals proved particularly costly, with Pochettino’s side missing the chance to take all three points despite Fernandes’ brace.

Mauricio Pochettino is still without a win after replacing Michael Carrick. Manchester United faces Brentford next with a hope of a first win for Pochettino.

#2048. Top 20 most valuable EFL League One strikers right now

Strikers are where the big money lies, and every club across the EFL wants their line-leaders to have high value.

In League One, that's no different, and with the third tier looking the tightest it's been in quite some time this season, a good number nine could end up being the difference between staying up or going down, mid-table or the play-offs, or maybe even going up automatically.

We saw last season how Leyton Orient's third-tier status was heavily preserved by Dom Ballard's goals and how the excellence of Bim Pepple and Lorent Tolaj drove a once hapless Plymouth Argyle side up the division in the second half of the season.

Two of those went for big money to Bristol City this past summer, but which current League One strikers could do the same?

According to Transfermarkt's data, these are the 20 strikers with the most value in the third tier right now.

N.B. All values are initially in Euros - converted to Pounds for the list

MK Dons re-signed Sam Nombe this past summer from Rotherham United for a guaranteed £600,000, which could surpass £1 million if add-ons are met.

The 28-year-old was bought when the Millers were in the Championship off the back of a 15-goal season with Exeter City, and then would score 14 and 12 in the last two seasons at the level in South Yorkshire, albeit last year ending in relegation.

That would have dropped his value, per Tranfsermarkt's ranks, but you'd expect another 10-goal season at least in this free-scoring MK side.

It's been a difficult few years for Gassan Ahadme. His value would have been sky-high after being signed for Charlton Athletic off the back of 11 goals in 29 third tier games for Cambridge United in 2023/24.

But, a couple of dud years, whether that be at the Valley in their promotion campaign, or last season at Stevenage, have lowered that back down, and now he's back at the Abbey, already with more league goals than he's managed in his last two seasons combined.

Bosnian frontman Admir Bristric was an intriguing signing for Leicester City to make this past summer. The 23-year-old scored 15 in 29 in all competitions last season for Slovenian side NK Bravo, and the Foxes paid at least €1.15m (£963k) for his services.

Unfortunately, Emil Riis signed less than a month later, and all of a sudden, Bristric was relegated to cameo roles and was quickly shunned out of League One plans.

His only appearances in the last three months have been in the EFL Trophy and the FA Cup against National League North side Oxford City. Even then, he only played three minutes off the bench against the sixth tier side.

Bristric is taking time getting used to the EFL, but if he remains out of Russell Martin's plans, his value will only decrease.

It's very impressive that Tom Bloxham, at only 23 years old, has 200 EFL appearances, most of which have come in League One. He's been, at worst, a useful squad player for around five years now, at Shrewsbury Town, Morecambe or now at Blackpool.

The towering six-foot-five frontman hasn't properly exploded into a 15-to-20-goal striker just yet in his career, but his duarability and potential contribute to Transfermarkt's value.

Perhaps the new Blackpool boss, once they're in the building, can start to get the best out of him.

Age does, unfortunately, have to play a factor in these values, as if Kyle Wootton was six years younger, he'd easily be worth double. He'd also probably be in the Championship, too.

Instead, the 30-year-old has to settle for being one of the best goalscoring big men in the third tier at Stockport County. He finished second in the Golden Boot ranks last season, but it's arguable that he'd have overtaken Dom Ballard if not for an injury crisis which meant he had to play centre-back for the final month of the campaign.

He's already in double digits this season, and is one of the key reasons why Stockport are so good under Jimmy McNulty, as his aerial threat means that they can go long to him if their patient build-up isn't working. Very valuable to the Hatters, but underrepresented on this list.

A position purely based on potential, Leeds United must be really disappointed that their 18-year-old starlet Harry Gray isn't currently excelling on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, and hasn't yet started a game under new boss Dave Challinor, as of writing.

The England Under-19 international is highly-rated both at Leeds and amongst general footballing circles, with him the latest line of Gray's, who are legendary at Elland Road.

The fact he was loaned out aged just 17 to Rotherham in January, instead of playing more youth football, just shows how developed he already is, and once Gray can finally get clicking at the top end of the pitch, his value will only climb higher.

Welsh international Mark Harris couldn't properly get going at Championship level with Oxford United following his 19-goal campaign in all competitions in 2023/24 to help the Yellows get promoted.

Now he's back in League One, though, his golscoring knack has returned. He's already netted more times than he has in each of his two seasons in the second-tier in the first few months of this term.

Transfermarkt's list shows a green arrow next to his £628k value, too, so it's increased since the start of the season.

Bojan Radulovic's value has definitely increased over the past 12 months or so. His Huddersfield Town career seemed to be over back in January 2025, when he was loaned out to Eredivisie side Fortuna Sittard after playing just 855 minutes of League One action.

He found form back at the Accu Stadium under Lee Grant, though, and netted seven in 15 appearances in the first half of last season. Unfortunately, in 2026, he's had an injury-ravaged year.

Radulovic missed lengthy periods towards the back end of last season, and this year has been in and out of the side under Martin Drury. Nevertheless, he still has a handful of league goals in limited minutes, and a full return would make an already threatening Terriers attack even better.

Someone else whose value has skyrocketed in recent times is Aaron Collins. Plainly put, not many were expecting him to have the year he's currently having based on last season's performances in League Two.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

The 29-year-old was one of the big-money MK Dons captures while they were in League Two, having netted at least 10 in three consecutive third tier seasons, but he only scored six league goals last year.

This season, though, he's scoring a goal a game in all competitions, leading the scoring charts in league action, and was awarded his Wales debut against Portugal in the latest round of Nations League games. Arguably, he could, and should, be even higher.

Jacob Brown was signed by Luton Town back in the summer of 2023 in their first campaign as a Premier League club. He'd netted Championship goals for Stoke City across the previous two seasons.

He's kind of lost his way since, like the Hatters have as a football club, in fairness, and after spending last season on loan up a level in the Championship with Portsmouth, he joined Reading on a free transfer at the end of his contract.

It's been a smart bit of business so far for Reading, with Brown one of, if not the best backup strikers in the division. Almost all of his appearances have been off the bench with Jack Marriott ahead of him, and he's still scored four times in league action as of writing.

#2045. Former winger wants selfish Bruno Fernandes to be sold and identifies replacement

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Despite a slow start to last season, Bruno Fernandes went on to finish the last season with 21 Premier League assists, breaking the competition’s single-season record.

This season has been a different situation. He isn’t at his usual best, contract talks have reported stalled and he publicy questioned Carrick’s tactics.

Bruno Fernandes has come under criticism for his performances and Ashley Young joins in as the latest to call for Bruno’s sale in January.

Manchester United have been told to cash in on Bruno Fernandes in January rather than offer the midfielder another contract. Meanwhile, Young identifies Morgan Gibbs-White as an upgrade over the Portuguese star.

The criticism of Fernandes has been particularly strong, with questions raised over his influence in central midfield.

“If Manchester United can cash in on him in January, I’d do that. I wouldn’t be looking to extend his contract at all. Keep him there, he’d be unhappy,” Ashley Young said while talking to BBC.

Young also questioned Fernandes’ attitude towards individual recognition, suggesting that winning personal awards appears to be an important part to his United career.

“He seems to me as a player that personal accolades are more important than the team. And that’s what he’s about. He’ll be looking at that, yeah, I want player of the year. I won player of the year. It was, it was me. You know, it weren’t my other teammates.”

The concerns were not limited to Fernandes’ attitude. His defensive positioning and the spaces he leaves behind when playing in central midfield were also highlighted.

The criticism comes from a view that opponents have regularly found opportunities to play through United’s midfield, particularly when Fernandes steps forward.

“I was at Everton teams, playing against Manchester United, and if he’s playing in central midfield, the tactic was, play through the midfield when you see them step out because there’s so much space in there. And it’s been the theme. It’s been the theme for years that Manchester United, if they play him in central midfield, there’s spaces all behind him.”

Ashley Young’s suggested alternative is Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White, who is believed to offer a different balance to the United midfield.

“I would go and get Morgan Gibbs-White if you can. And I’d go and do it in January. For me, I think Morgan Gibbs-White would give more to that team than what Bruno Fernandes is now.”

It would be a major decision for United if they let him go. There is no doubt on his quality as he has scored 113 goals in 341 appearances since arriving from Sporting in 2020.

However, his future has become a talking point after United reportedly saw two contract offers rejected. Fernandes is understood to want a four-year agreement, while the club remain cautious about committing to such a deal with the midfielder already 32.

With Mauricio Pochettino in the dugout now and reportedly involved in his contract negotiations, the upcoming months can be very different for Manchester United and Bruno Fernandes.

He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Joshua Zirkzee believes Manchester United should take responsibility for their failure to beat Sporting on Wednesday rather than blame referee Szymon Marciniak.

Mauricio Pochettino’s side had two goals disallowed during the 2-2 Champions League draw in Lisbon. Bruno Fernandes scored twice against his former club early in the second half to put United ahead. However, an error by goalkeeper Senne Lammens allowed Luis Suarez to equalise with 10 minutes remaining.

“We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead,” Zirkzee told MUTV. Although frustrated by some of Marciniak’s decisions, the Dutchman felt United had sufficient quality to win the game regardless.

Wednesday’s appearance was Zirkzee’s first start for United since May’s goalless draw at Sunderland. The forward benefited from Matheus Cunha’s European suspension and received considerable vocal support from the travelling fans in Lisbon.

Zirkzee was replaced after 64 minutes, with Bryan Mbeumo moving into the centre-forward position. With Cunha available again for Saturday’s visit of Brentford, Pochettino has a decision to make over the composition of his attack.

United’s improvement in Lisbon was evident, particularly during the opening stages of the second half. However, their inability to protect a winning position ultimately proved more costly than any decision made by Marciniak.

Pochettino is still awaiting his first victory as United manager, something Zirkzee is clearly anxious to help deliver against Brentford.

#2042. Chris Wilder urged to make 'controversial' Tom Cannon exit decision at Sheffield United

It has been an excellent start to the season for Sheffield United in the Championship.

After a summer of off-field uncertainty that saw the departures of key players such as Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer, it is fair to say Sheffield United supporters went into the season with low expectations, but Chris Wilder's men have certainly surprised many with their strong start.

After scoring a 90th-minute equaliser to salvage a point in a 1-1 draw with Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night, Sheffield United are ninth in the Championship table, just one point from the play-off places.

As the Blades continue their impressive form, hopes of a potential promotion push will be increasing in S2, but one man who may not be enjoying his current situation is striker Tom Cannon.

Cannon joined United from Leicester City in January 2025 for a reported fee of around £10 million, but he has scored just 11 goals in 73 appearances during what has been a frustrating near two-year spell at the club.

The 23-year-old has netted three times in 16 games this season, but just nine of those appearances have come from the start, and on what was just his second start in the past month against the Saints in midweek, he was replaced by Patrick Bamford at half time.

Cannon was linked with a return to two of his former loan clubs in the summer, Preston North End and Stoke City, but, speaking in September, the striker denied that he was keen to make a move elsewhere.

When asked which player the club should loan out in January, FLW's Sheffield United fan pundit Jimmy, from the YouTube channel Blades Ramble, claimed that Cannon could benefit from a temporary move, either to boost his confidence ahead of a return to Bramall Lane or increase his value before a potential sale.

"It's slightly controversial this one because I'm not sure how many would agree, but I think that Tom Cannon needs a loan away," Jimmy told FLW.

"Some Blades may have given up on him already and would like to get a fee for him because strikers obviously go for a premium, but I don't think his value would be that high at the moment.

"I think there's potential that he goes elsewhere and does well.

"He could be offered out on loan to the Championship, and then, if he does well, it certainly raises his price, but we would also have the option of bringing him back into the fold at United, where he's still got years to run on his contract.

"He could play a part for us or we could sell him on for a higher price than we'd get now.

"I would be looking at potentially getting Tom Cannon some confidence under his belt by sending him out on loan."

Football League World takes a closer look at the best value-for-money signings in the Championship this season

Despite his underwhelming form throughout his time at the club, Wilder has always been publicly supportive of Cannon, and the Sheffield United boss may be reluctant to give up on a player he has devoted plenty of time to developing.

However, almost two years into his spell at Bramall Lane, Cannon is showing no sign of delivering the prolific form the Blades would have been expecting when they paid an eight-figure fee for his services, so Wilder may soon have a big decision to make.

Does Tom Cannon deserve more time at Sheffield United or should the Blades cut their losses? Tell us in the comments below!

Cannon performed better during his loan stints at Preston and Stoke than he has after his permanent moves to Leicester and Sheffield United, so if the South Yorkshire outfit are keen to recoup some of their money, sending him out on loan could be the perfect way to put him in the shop window.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2041. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2040. Stockport County vs Leyton Orient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 15:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:05

Looking to remain top of the League One table heading into the final month of the year, Stockport County welcome Leyton Orient to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Hatters currently hold a three-point lead at the summit after recording their third consecutive victory with a 3-0 win away to Cambridge United, while the O's are hoping to close the gap on the playoff places after beating AFC Wimbledon 4-1 last time out.

Following their agonisingly narrow failure to secure promotion to the Championship last season, Stockport County parted ways with long-serving manager Dave Challinor and appointed former Rochdale boss Jimmy McNulty as his replacement.

McNulty has so far overseen 21 matches in charge of the Hatters across all competitions, recording 13 wins, four draws and four defeats to give him an impressive win rate of 61.9%.

Ten of those victories have come in League One, with Stockport looking to enter December at the top of the table after collecting 32 points from their opening 16 matches, a lead they could extend to six points if results elsewhere go their way and they secure a fourth consecutive league win.

Their impressive league form has also carried over into the cup competitions, with McNulty's men finishing top of their EFL Trophy group and booking their place in the next round of the FA Cup, although they survived a major scare earlier this month, coming from two goals behind to beat Isthmian League side Cray Wanderers 3-2.

More recently, the Greater Manchester outfit climbed to the summit of League One with an emphatic 3-0 victory over Cambridge, a match that featured a superb free-kick from captain Oliver Norwood.

The three goals scored last weekend took Stockport's league tally to 32 for the season, a total bettered by no other side in the third tier and only three teams across England's top four divisions.

As for visitors Leyton Orient, they have enjoyed a more consistent campaign this time around after spending much of the 2025-26 season battling near the bottom of the table and ultimately finishing just one place above the relegation zone.

After their opening 14 League One matches, the London-based side sit 12th under the continued leadership of Richie Wellens, who recently surpassed 250 games in charge of the O's, with six wins, two draws and six defeats leaving them on 20 points.

Although victory on Saturday, at a ground where Stockport boast the best home record in the division, would not be enough to lift Orient into the playoff places, it could leave them just three points outside the top six, with games in hand over all but one of the teams currently above them.

The O's most recently continued their impressive home form with a convincing 4-1 victory over London neighbours AFC Wimbledon, securing their fourth league win in their last five matches at Brisbane Road.

In fact, Wellens' side are already closing in on surpassing their total number of home victories from the whole of last season, having won half of their league fixtures on home soil so far in 2026-27.

Although the two sides finished at opposite ends of the table last season, neither could claim bragging rights in their meetings, with both encounters ending in draws.

The last time either side won this fixture within 90 minutes was in February 2025, the same season they faced each other in the League One playoff semi-finals.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Hoping to make it six consecutive victories in all competitions, McNulty will be keen to stick with his winning formula and has the option to do so after his side came through their latest fixture without any fresh injury concerns.

Norwood is expected to retain his place in midfield, while club top scorer Kyle Wootton will lead the line as he looks to add to his 10 League One goals this season, with Jack Diamond operating out wide.

Leyton Orient also look set to travel from the capital with the option of naming an unchanged starting XI following last weekend's victory.

Former Tottenham Hotspur forward Dane Scarlett is expected to lead the line again after scoring in consecutive matches, while Alex Gilbert should retain his place in midfield after scoring and providing an assist against Wimbledon.

Wellens will, however, remain without Ollie O'Neill, who is expected to miss four months after undergoing surgery shortly after returning from a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare are also expected to remain in the treatment room.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Gordon, O'Connell, Pye; Glover, Bate, Norwood, Ennis; Diamond, Wootton, Wood

Baxter; Stevens, Gilchrist, Edmonds-Green, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, C. Wellens, Dobra; Scarlett

Although Leyton Orient have produced some encouraging results in recent weeks, we expect the league leaders to show why they sit at the top of the table and maintain their push for promotion.

We see Stockport having enough quality to extend their impressive home record and make it four consecutive league victories.

#2038. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

#2036. Senegal Knockout Tie Gives Chelsea A Double Xabi Alonso Audit

Chelsea’s World Cup watch has moved beyond simple minutes management.

Senegal’s Round-of-32 meeting with Belgium now gives Xabi Alonso a live read on two very different development tracks.

Nicolas Jackson’s attacking authority is the immediate question. Mamadou Sarr’s defensive readiness is the longer-term one.

Chelsea confirmed that Senegal kept their knockout hopes alive with a 5-0 win over Iraq, with Jackson featuring from the bench.

Senegal have since moved into the knockouts, where they face Belgium in Seattle on Wednesday 1 July.

Jackson and Sarr travel into that game with contrasting club questions attached. Both still carry clear Chelsea relevance.

Sarr has not been the loudest Chelsea story of the tournament.

That may actually make this test more useful.

The 20-year-old is still moving through the awkward stage between prospect, squad option and saleable BlueCo asset.

Knockout football against Belgium can sharpen that picture quickly.

The timing is awkward in the best possible way for Chelsea. Alonso steps into a squad with expensive centre-backs, academy-trained options and a board still comfortable using the market aggressively.

A disciplined Sarr performance would not end that search. It would give the recruitment team a stronger internal benchmark before committing another major fee.

Chelsea need defenders who can hold a high line, cover wide channels and still pass through pressure. Belgium should ask those questions more directly than most group-stage opponents.

The context matters. Chelsea’s recall note recorded that Sarr returned from Strasbourg after 18 appearances across Ligue 1 and the Conference League.

The club also noted that he had already earned his first Senegal cap.

That is a different profile from an academy player being carried by reputation alone.

There is a statistical base behind the interest too. When Chelsea completed the deal, beIN SPORTS noted that Sarr made 27 Ligue 1 appearances in his first Strasbourg season.

He helped them keep 10 clean sheets. He also produced a team-high 20 blocks and made 25 interceptions.

Those numbers explain why this Belgium game is not just a sentimental World Cup subplot.

Alonso’s Chelsea defence is already crowded with Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and external targets still orbiting the plan.

ReadChelsea has already looked at why Colwill’s recovery story gives Alonso a defensive test. Sarr’s value is different.

He is still being evaluated as a physical, long-range defensive project.

Jackson’s role changes the editorial weight of the tie.

Chelsea’s striker picture has been messy for long enough. Any high-pressure international performance now carries wider meaning.

ReadChelsea has already framed the forward’s tournament as a live Senegal striker audit for Chelsea.

Belgium should stress both Chelsea questions at once.

Jackson has to offer penalty-box threat and transition security. Sarr, if trusted, has to defend space against a technically cleaner opponent.

He also has to show whether his recovery pace and frame translate under tournament pressure.

Sarr’s own mentality profile is worth noting. In a Chelsea World Cup Q&A, he named Lionel Messi, Sadio Mane and Paul Pogba as his tournament heroes.

His answer on Pogba focused on leadership and group mentality.

That lands neatly with the exact question Chelsea now need answered. Is there enough presence to go with the physical tools?

This is why Belgium feels like a pathway check rather than a routine World Cup watch item.

Chelsea do not need Sarr to solve the defence in July. They need clearer evidence on whether he belongs in Alonso’s first pre-season group.

He could need another loan. He could also become part of the club’s centre-back market arithmetic.

For Jackson, the question is more immediate. For Sarr, it is more structural.

Together, Senegal’s knockout tie gives Chelsea a rare clean look at two players on opposite ends of the same squad-building argument.

Who can help now, and who is worth protecting for later?

#2034. Chelsea news: Xabi Alonso slams Wesley Fofana for interview comments

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:13

Xabi Alonso has revealed that Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for comments made in an interview earlier this week.

The Blues are currently preparing for a Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Sitting in eighth place in the Premier League table after three defeats in four matches, Alonso could have done without any controversy away from the pitch.

Instead, Fofana gave an interview where he revealed that he considered retirement during a prolonged spell on the sidelines with serious knee injuries.

Not only did the Frenchman add that he was convinced to continue playing by his agent because of the money he could earn, Fofana hinted that he was not overly disappointed to miss a spot kick in a penalty shootout against Liverpool last month.

Addressing the situation at a press conference, Alonso suggested that he had been left furious by Fofana's words.

He told reporters: "Absolutely, we have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate.

"He apologised, he knows it was not right the moment, it was not right the content, we are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated and we know that it's something that we don't want, these kind of things and they are not going to be repeated for sure."

The Spaniard added that he now regarded the matter as "closed", indicating that Fofana remains available to face Forest.

Fofana's place in the Chelsea defence had already been in doubt due to the level of his performance in the 4-1 defeat versus Leeds last weekend.

Although there have been games this season where the 25-year-old has played to an acceptable standard, his attitude and decision-making in the Chelsea backline has been questioned for months.

Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury has led to Fofana partnering Levi Colwill, but they have performed poorly both individually and as a partnership.

Alonso may consider using Josh Acheampong alongside Colwill versus Forest, but that could potentially cause issues at full-back.

#2033. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.
